questions.stem: What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves.

options.label: B
options.text: They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors.

options.label: C
options.text: They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases.

options.label: D
options.text: They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage 问的是文章"告诉我们
什么"，属于事实查询，不是推断。
【拆句】What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage 句式为 "learn about X
from Y"——从 Y 中了解到关于 X 的什么；about 后是话题，from 后是来源。结构平铺直
叙，无陷阱。
【定位】While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be
identified by genetic testing alone.
虽然某些罕见疾病能轻松识别出来，但大多数潜在的健康问题靠基因检测一项是查不出
来的。
【选项】A) 与原文相反
They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves 用 certain
（某些）替换原文的 most（多数）——原文恰恰说 certain rare diseases can be
easily identified，让步从句中的 certain rare 反而是"能识别的"，A 把它颠倒了。
B) 无中生有
They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors 凭空加
了"区分基因与非基因因素"这件事——原文只说健康状况受非基因因素影响，从未要求
基因检测"区分"两者。
C) ✓ 正确
most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone ↔
They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases
predict 关键的"多数""靠它单独"两个限定词，C 选项用 the majority of 和
independently 一一对应，且主语"基因健康检测"一致，无任何过度信息。
D) 偷换概念
They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment 把
lifestyle 和 environment 单挑出来谈区分，但原文这两词只是 non-genetic factors,
such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others 的举例，且 also 之后从未谈"区
分两者影响"。
questions.locateHint: While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be

questions.stem: What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret?

options.label: A
options.text: The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene.

options.label: B
options.text: The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact.

options.label: C
options.text: The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones.

options.label: D
options.text: The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题）
【判型】What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret 是 What makes
X Y 的句式，问的是事实层面的原因，原文里有现成原因句。
【拆句】What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret 结构是 "make +
宾语 + 形容词"——"使...变得难以解读"。What 作主语，问的是导致这件难事的原因；to
interpret 是后置不定式作形容词补足语。
【定位】A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together.
一次基因检测可以同时查看许多基因，但很难预测这些基因放在一起会怎么"协作"。
【选项】A) 偷换概念
The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene 把"每个单基因的作
用"塞进答案，但 each contributing a little to the outcome 只是顺带一提"每个贡献
一点"，原文并没有说"难以确定每个基因的作用"。
B) ✓ 正确
it's difficult to predict how they will play together ↔
The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact
整篇文章只有 P6 这一句用了 difficult to predict 的结构，预判"基因互动难以预测"严
丝合缝地对应 B 选项的"预测基因如何相互作用的难度"，直接锁定。
C) 无中生有
The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones 编出"区分基因
因素与环境因素"这件事——原文只说"还要把非基因因素也考虑进去"，从未要求"区分
两者"。
D) 无中生有
The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved 把焦点放到"识别
这几百个基因的庞大工作量"——原文 hundreds of genes 只是说数量大，没说"识别它
们工作量巨大"，也根本没说"工作量"才是"难解读"的原因。
questions.locateHint: A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents?

options.label: A
options.text: They are solid scientific bases for application.

options.label: B
options.text: They are helpful in finding a romantic match.

options.label: C
options.text: They do not look promising at the moment.

options.label: D
options.text: They do not make any sense at present.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （态度题）
【判型】What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents——配
合选项里 do not look promising、do not make any sense 这种全是态度评价的格局，本
质是问作者对这件事的态度。
【拆句】What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents 中
"DNA tests to predict ..." 的不定式 to predict 作 DNA tests 的后置定语，等于 "DNA
tests that predict ..."——"用来预测人格或才能的 DNA 测试"。
【定位】Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality
or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. At the moment, the scientific bases for these
applications are non-existent or incredibly weak.
那些声称能帮你找到完美恋爱对象的检测、以及那些号称能根据 DNA 预测性格或才能的检
测，都是纯粹的胡说八道。眼下，这些应用的科学依据要么压根不存在，要么薄弱得离谱。
【选项】A) 与原文相反
They are solid scientific bases for application 说"是坚实的科学依据"，原文恰好说
the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak
——科学依据要么不存在要么极弱，方向完全相反。
B) 与原文相反
They are helpful in finding a romantic match 抓了原文里的另一个例子 find your
perfect romantic match——但原文是把它当作"也是胡说"的反面例子，B 却说它"有帮
助"，立场反了。
C) 偷换概念
They do not look promising at the moment 译过来是"目前看起来不太有前景"——
但原文是 pure nonsense（纯属胡扯），属于强烈否定，C 把它弱化成"前景不佳"这种
中性偏负的客气说法。
D) ✓ 正确
are pure nonsense ↔ They do not make any sense at present
At the moment ↔ at present
预判"作者强烈否定"对应 do not make any sense；at present 又把 at the moment
这个时间限定带上了——D 一字不漏地把作者的核心态度搬过来了。
questions.locateHint: Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality

title: 2025年12月真题·第2套 · 选词填空

paragraphs.text: Some music inspires you to move your feet, some inspires you to get out there and change the world. In any case, it's  [26]  to say that music moves people in special ways.
If you're especially into a piece of music, your brain does something called Autonomous Sensory Meridian Response (ASMR), which  [27]  to you like a sting in your brain.

It turns out that ASMR is pretty special. According to a  [28]  published study in The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease, the part of your brain responsible for ASMR doesn't get lost to Alzheimer's. Alzheimer's  [29]  to put people into layers of confusion, and the study confirms that music can sometimes  [30]  lift people out of the Alzheimer's haze and bring them back to (at least a likeness of) normality … if only for a short while. ASMR is powerful stuff!

This phenomenon has been  [31]  several times but rarely studied properly. One of the most famous examples of this is the story of 92-year-old Henry Dryer, who comes out of dementia(痴呆) while listening to songs from his youth.

Jeff Anderson, associate professor in Radiology at the University of Utah and  [32]  author on the study, says "In our society, the diagnoses of dementia are  [33]  resources to the maximum. No one says playing music will be a cure for Alzheimer's disease, but it might make the symptoms more  [34]  , decrease the cost of care and improve a patient's  [35]  of life."

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】D) fair
形容词
【词性槽】it's ___ to say that …，形式主语 it 后系动词 + 表语
【依据】It's fair to say 是英语高频习语「可以这样说、说……不为过」
it's __(26)__ to say that music moves people in special ways. 前文用「有些音乐让你想
跳舞，有些激励你改变世界」铺陈，再来一句「可以说音乐以特别的方式打动人心」做总
结，正是 it's fair to say 的标准用法。
【竞争词】F) manageable manageable 修饰「可控、可处理」，和 to say 接不上
manageable 通常修饰任务、症状（make symptoms more manageable），用来说一件事
「可控」；说一句话「可控」语义荒谬。
M) taxing taxing 是「费神的」，说一句话费神在语境里不通
taxing 多修饰任务、工作量；it's taxing to say 字面虽通，但与前文铺陈「音乐打动人」的语气
完全相反，开篇就泼冷水不合逻辑。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】E) feels
动词
【词性槽】your brain does … which ___ to you like a sting，which 引导的定语从句缺谓语
【依据】feel like 是固定搭配「感觉像」
which __(27)__ to you like a sting in your brain 后面跟 like a sting（像针刺），feels
(to you) like … 正是「（对你来说）感觉像……」的标准表达，对人称 sb. 用 feels to sb.
like 也通。
【竞争词】G) mends mend 是「修补」，与 like a sting 不搭
mend 通常修补衣服、关系，无法「mend to you like a sting」，搭配和语义都不成立。
N) tends tend 后接 to do，不接 to you like
tends 常见结构是 tends to do sth.（往往做某事），后面接动词原形；这里后面是介词 to you
+ like + 名词，结构对不上。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】L) recently
副词
【词性槽】a ___ published study，冠词与过去分词之间填副词修饰 published
【依据】recently published「最近发表」是学术文献标配搭配
According to a __(28)__ published study，引用研究时强调「最近发表的一项研究」是英
语中极高频的表达 a recently published study；时间副词 recently 与 published 在意义
上紧密呼应。
【竞争词】A) actually actually 表「实际上」，修饰 published 语义空洞
actually published「实际上发表的」在英语里几乎不用——研究要么发表了要么没有，没有
「实际上发表」这种说法，搭配不自然。
B) consequently consequently 表因果，前文无因，逻辑不接
consequently 用来连接前因后果，这里 According to a … published study 是引出依据，并非
承接因果；且 a consequently published study 不是英语习惯搭配。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 A) —— L 还是 A？三个副词都「看着能用」。a __(28)__
published study 中考生可能凭直觉填 actually 表「实际上发表」，但英语习惯是 recently
published；防坑点：a + 时间副词 + V-ed 名词是学术语境的强搭配模板，时间副词优先
于强调副词。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】N) tends
动词
【词性槽】Alzheimer's ___ to put people …，主语后缺谓语，第三人称单数
【依据】tends to do 表「倾向于、往往」，契合阿尔茨海默症常见症状
Alzheimer's __(29)__ to put people into layers of confusion，「阿尔茨海默症往往让人
陷入层层困惑」，tends to 表常发性、规律性，符合医学论述的口吻。
【竞争词】G) mends mend 不接 to do，且语义反向
mend 是「修补、痊愈」，不接 to do；而且 Alzheimer's mends people 意思是「阿尔茨海默
症治愈人」，与下文「陷入困惑」完全矛盾。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】A) actually
副词
【词性槽】music can sometimes ___ lift people out of …，情态动词 + 副词 + 实义动词
【依据】actually 强调「真的、的确」，呼应前文研究证实
the study confirms that music can sometimes __(30)__ lift people out of the
Alzheimer's haze，研究「证实」音乐有时确实能把患者从混沌中拉出来，actually 强调这
种效果是真实存在的，与 confirms 的语气一致。
【竞争词】B) consequently consequently 是因果连接副词，本句无因果链
consequently 通常放句首/分句首引出结果（…, consequently, …）；这里没有「因为某事 →
所以 lift」的因果，硬塞进 can sometimes consequently lift 既不合习惯也不合逻辑。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】H) observed
动词
【词性槽】This phenomenon has been ___ several times，被动语态，has been + 过去分词
【依据】observed「被观察到」与并列的 studied 同属研究动作
This phenomenon has been __(31)__ several times but rarely studied properly. 中 but
连接转折，前后都讲科研动作：「被观察到多次，却很少被认真研究」，observed 与
studied 是天然的近义并列。
【竞争词】O) yielded yield 不及物或表「产生/屈服」，与 phenomenon 主语不搭
yield 表「产生（结果）」时用法是 A yielded B；表「屈服」时是 yield to。This
phenomenon has been yielded 字面意思「这种现象被产生了」语义荒谬，主被动语义都对
不上。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】C) contributing
形容词
【词性槽】___ author on the study，冠词位 + 名词 author 前作定语
【依据】contributing author 是学术文献固定身份「参与撰写的作者」
associate professor in Radiology at the University of Utah and __(32)__ author on the
study，介绍 Jeff Anderson 的双重身份，「副教授」+「该研究的参与撰写作者」逻辑自
然；contributing author 是学术论文署名中的标准说法。
【竞争词】J) plotting plotting 是「密谋/绘图」，修饰 author 语义荒诞
plotting author 字面是「正在密谋的作者」或「在画图的作者」，作为学术身份描述完全不
通；学术场合无此搭配。
M) taxing taxing 形容「繁重的」，不能用来形容人的身份
taxing 通常修饰任务、工作（a taxing job），用来形容 author（人）逻辑不通，且语义偏负
面，与正面介绍学者的语境冲突。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】M) taxing
动词
【词性槽】the diagnoses of dementia are ___ resources，be 动词后缺谓语成分，与后面
resources 形成动宾
【依据】tax resources「使资源吃紧」是固定搭配，与 to the maximum 呼应
the diagnoses of dementia are __(33)__ resources to the maximum，「痴呆诊断正在
最大限度地消耗资源」；tax 作动词意为「使……负担沉重」，tax resources 在医疗/财政语
境是标准说法，to the maximum「到极限」直接强化这种「榨干资源」的意味。
【竞争词】J) plotting plot resources 不是搭配，且语义对不上「占用资源」
plot 表「策划/绘制」，plot resources 字面像「策划资源、绘制资源」，与「消耗社会资源」
的语境完全错位。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 J) —— M 还是 J？「熟词僻义」盲区。are __(33)__ resources to
the maximum 中考生若不知 tax 还有动词义「使吃紧」，会怀疑 taxing，转去试
plotting；防坑点：看到 resources、energy、patience 等被「耗」对象，taxing 比
plotting 自然得多，平时多积累一词多义。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】F) manageable
形容词
【词性槽】make the symptoms more ___，make + 宾语 + 形容词比较级，空填形容词
【依据】make symptoms more manageable「让症状更可控」医学语境标配
it might make the symptoms more __(34)__, decrease the cost of care and improve a
patient's __(35)__ of life.，三件好事并列：症状更可控、护理成本下降、生活质量提升；
manageable 与「降低成本、改善质量」语气完全一致。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】K) quality
名词
【词性槽】improve a patient's ___ of life，所有格+of 锁定名词
【依据】quality of life 是英语固定搭配
improve a patient's __(35)__ of life 中，quality of life「生活质量」是医学/社科语境里的
高频固定表达，与前文 decrease the cost of care 并列，逻辑顺。
【竞争词】I) phase phase of life 偏「人生阶段」，与「改善」不搭
phase of life 表示「人生的某个阶段」，可以「进入」一个 phase 但谈不上 improve a phase
of life；这里要的是生活的「品质」可以被提升，phase 在搭配上和语义上都对不上。

title: 2025年12月真题·第2套 · 长篇匹配（Can playing video games ）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The gaming industry is larger than films and music combined, yet few of us are likely to list our achievements in playing computer games as work experience in our résumé. But why not? Businesses are waking up to the skills gamers can bring to the workplace.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: One start-up is convinced that the skills learned by playing games — hard-won through years of training and battle — can be applied to real-life work situations. And Game Academy reckons its belief is backed up by hard data. Do you enjoy unusual puzzle games like Portal, or tower defence games like Defense Grid? The team has found that IT workers play those more than average. But if you prefer Civilization, Total War, or X-Com, where strategy and resource management are key, then you might have more in common with managers.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Game Academy's idea is simple: analyse gamers' habits from their online gaming profile, and offer courses in valuable skills that reflect their aptitudes — skills they can practise and refine in-game. And there is already a growing acceptance that gaming skills are transferable.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Even the military is hiring gamers. "The ability to absorb information, react swiftly and coordinate actions whilst remaining calm under pressure are often attributes of people that are good at gaming," according to a Royal Air Force spokesperson. Those skills are part of what the Royal Air Force is looking for "in a variety of roles". "Skills acquired through gaming can be very relevant to certain areas."

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "There are plenty of soft skills that gamers can utilise in a professional setting, such as teamwork, problem solving and strategic planning," says Ryan Gardner, a regional director with Hays recruitment. But does that really mean your top 100 ranking in Overwatch should go down in your résumé? "It's about how you either make it relevant to the job you are applying for, or how it makes you more interesting as a potential employee," Mr Gardner says.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Two years ago, a Glasgow University study made headlines for suggesting gaming could make students more successful. But "the research hasn't really changed minds, at least not yet," says one of the authors of the study, Dr Matthew Barr. He's now writing a book on the topic. "For now, I think the negative reputation around games means that telling someone you're a determined gamer is more likely to harm your chances of getting a job. But if someone can explain how they've led a team in an online game, for example, they may be able to persuade an employer that this is useful," says Dr Barr.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Playing games casually is unlikely to help your career prospects. But part of Game Academy's suggestion is to transform casual gamers into "conscious" ones, applying critical thinking to developing their skills. "We see gameplay as a resource of talent," says co-founder David Barrie. "Why can't we put in our résumé our gaming victories and achievements?" he asks. "If they say they want leadership — why can't I point to my years of leading World of Warcraft raids?"

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: There are already plenty of gamers out there who know that their hobby has made them who they are. Earlier this year, Matthew Ricci told gaming site Kotaku: "If you're playing EVE Online you basically already have an MBA." Often made fun of in gaming circles as a "spreadsheet simulator(电子表格模拟)", the economy of the fictional EVE universe is driven by real market principles. If you want to build a new spaceship, the raw material has to be mined by another player. Manufacturing costs come into effect, and commodities fluctuate in price based on demand and the distance to haul the commodity.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Mr Ricci, who had always dreamed of being the boss of his own company, ran an in-game corporation comprising hundreds of players. Eventually, he realised he could transfer his skills to real-life business — instead of doing it for free. He restructured Zentech, once a taxation vehicle for his father's business, and it is now in its fourth year helping international brands enter the Canadian market. EVE teaches skills like creativity, leadership, organisation, and conflict resolution, he maintains. He credits his success to his family, his strong desire to run his own business — and "a damn good company in Iceland that made a damn good game".

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Digital entrepreneur and business consultant Mia Bennett says: "In more traditional settings, gaming is still imagined to be the pursuit of teenage boys — a waste of time." But there are some links to skills like "decision-making, the ability to anticipate and future planning," she says. "It also helps with meta-skills — learning how to learn, experimentation, and creative thinking."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Twelve years into his career, Mark Long, a radiotherapy physicist with the NHS in Surrey, doesn't get as much gaming time as he used to. "I would love to say that my gaming skills allow me to destroy cancer using linear accelerators like photon(光子) blasters, but that's not quite the reality." Instead, he credits old-school games like Palace of Magic with exposing him to computers. Every new gaming upgrade improved his knowledge of how they worked. Gaming also encouraged a competitive spirit — and that, he believes, translates. "When creating treatment plans, the aim is to optimise the radiation dose to the tumour and restrict it as much as possible to healthy surrounding tissues and organs," he says. It's about "repeating the process, but each time doing something slightly different to improve the result". Not unlike achieving a high score or a perfect run. "Most videogames are essentially puzzles to solve," he says. "And problem-solving is a big part of my job."

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: "Over at Game Academy, Mr Barrie is aware they still have a mountain to climb. The employer community will need the science," he says, but confesses he only became a true believer when he started asking players about their biggest in-game achievements. "The scale and scope of their answers were amazing," he says. "But ask them the same about their work, and they don't know." "The engagement and powerful skills that people get playing a game — why can't work be like that?" he asks.

paragraphs.text: Junk food is now a staple of many Americans' diets. Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. Bad diets are.

Interventions(干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers. Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat. Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach.

Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice.

To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy. The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm for these vulnerable groups. Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to "fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food"

After the intervention, participants associated healthy eating with autonomy and social justice. The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing. Importantly, there were also some promising effects of the new intervention on actual behavior. A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. The teens chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) more often over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda). Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity.

title: 2025年12月真题·第2套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.

But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages.

Since your baby doesn't dream at this stage of brain development, it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.

Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? Good question, but the answer is nothing! So, when do babies start dreaming? The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.
Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.

Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots(快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. According to Foulkes, "Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration." Kids ages 5 – 9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. Still, that's not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.
So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.

title: 2025年12月真题·第1套 · 长篇匹配（The battle over bike lan）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Five years ago, the city of Queens, New York, announced that it would be putting bike lanes onto a stretch of Skillman Ave — and removing 116 parking spots. Cyclists loved the plan, but local business owners got very angry. Taking out those parking spots, as they argued at protests and in letters to the city council, would ruin stores and restaurants along Skillman. "Parking here is already a nightmare," one shouted at a protest rally.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: But the bike lanes were a done deal, and soon they were in place. Early this year, Jesse Coburn — an investigative writer with Streetsblog New York — wondered whether those predictions of economic collapse came true. So he asked the city's Department of Finance to give him a few years' worth of sales figures for that stretch of Skillman Ave. How had the businesses on that street fared?

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Quite well, it turns out. In the year after the bike lanes arrived, businesses on Skillman saw sales rise by 12 percent, compared to 3 percent for Queens in general. What's more, that section of road saw new businesses open, while Queens overall had a net loss.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The thing is, the actual merchants along Skillman? They didn't believe it. When Coburn spoke to them and described what he'd found, only a few store owners admitted the lanes had helped. Many still insisted the lanes were killing their part of the city. And emotions ran hot: Someone scattered tacks(大头钉) on the bike lane.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: This little story turns out to be a fascinating glimpse at the challenges cities face as they try to update their urban infrastructure — to clean up the air, reduce greenhouse emissions, and speed up travel by making towns more bike-friendly. There's a rising amount of data showing that installing bike lanes and making streets more pedestrian-friendly boosts the economic fortunes of a place. Removing cars and parking spots works. But the folks who run local businesses simply aren't convinced, even when their own street performs. Given that sort of mess, can political fights over bike lanes ever end?

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: In 2013, researchers at New York City's Department of Transportation studied seven stretches of road that had installed bike lanes or created pedestrian-friendly areas. The city analyzed the data for businesses along those routes and found that by the third year, sales grew faster on five of the streets than in the district overall, on average — up to five times faster, in fact.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Beyond New York, a survey of research from 23 cities found that bike lanes and pedestrian-friendly design didn't hurt local retail and food stores. ("Fears of disastrous consequences for local businesses are unfounded," the researchers concluded.) More recent work has shown roughly the same.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The truth is that in fairly dense areas, bikes are more efficient at moving people around. You might lose one car driver's business — but you gain shoppers who now can arrive more easily on bikes. "Cyclists and pedestrians are consumers too," notes Professor Susan Handy. Plus, streets redesigned for bikes and pedestrians tend to become more pleasant places to hang around, so "in a lot of cases, that's created much nicer environments that are really good for those businesses."

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Mom-and-pop shops are usually pretty quick at recognizing situations that will help their bottom lines. So why the blind spot here? Perhaps it's that attention focuses on horror stories — and some merchants do get hit when bike lanes come in.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: I spoke to Cindy Hughes, a hairdresser(理发师) in Cambridge, Massachusetts. She said business fell by at least 40 percent when the city removed nearby parking to put in a bike lane. The majority of her customers drive, with many coming from nearby towns. Only a very few have shifted to cycling, and even those almost certainly won't cycle in Boston's snowy winters. So while Hughes supports bike lanes — "cyclists deserve to be safe" — she sees the parking loss as an existential risk. "Look, 90 percent of my customers drive," she told me. "For our business, the bike lanes are way worse than Covid was."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: For others, the pushback is cultural, says Henry Grabar, a writer for the Slate Magazine. Small business owners are frequently drivers who commute from other parts of the city by car, Grabar points out. They're also often longtime locals. "They tend to be people with deep roots in the city, who have hung around since before the neighborhood became what it is today," he adds. Driving around town in a car is so normal to them that cycling seems weird and unusual — despite its boost from Covid, when bike sales exploded by 75 percent.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Psychology beats all! Who knew, right? The fierce divide between store owners and bike-lane advocates seems similar to our larger culture wars over climate change. If we've learned anything about culture wars, it's that data isn't much good at changing minds.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: When Janette Sadik-Khan was the head of New York City's Transportation Department back in the early 2000s, she oversaw a rollout(推出) of bike lanes — and got angry blowback from residents and business owners who claimed there weren't enough cyclists to justify installing lanes. Now, she notes ironically, the lanes are so full of activity that opponents have turned to claiming the problem is the opposite: There are too many cyclists getting in the way of cars.

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: Maybe bike lanes will always be charged with emotion, until enough of the public is finally concerned about climate change — and it seems reckless(鲁莽的) to not have them.

paragraphs.label: O
paragraphs.text: Crises, after all, have a way of opening people's eyes to possibilities. During Covid, restaurants and cafés lost so much business that cities nationwide began allowing them to build curbside seating areas where people could sit, safely, in the open air. It greatly reduced parking — but because, well, shop owners didn't see any way around it. Customers loved the outdoor seating so much that cities are making it permanent: A New York City study of several streets closed during Covid found storeowners making more than before, and diners enjoying the outdoor lifestyle. If data won't change minds, customers might.

title: 2025年12月真题·第1套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: All living organisms on Earth are exposed to a 24-hour day-night cycle. This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day. Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health. For example, eating at night can lead to weight gain over time because food intake at night leads to increased fat storage.

Many drug targets in the body follow a 24-hour cycle, too. This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period. Because how the body responds to a drug can differ depending on the time it is taken, it logically follows that taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects.

When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it. There are two main reasons for that oversight. First, many physicians are not aware that some drugs work better during a specific time of the day. And second, most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle. Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance.

Over 50 years ago, researchers found that the cholesterol drug simvastatin is more effective at lowering cholesterol levels when taken at night rather than during the day. This is because the liver enzyme(酶) these drugs target is more active at night.

Taking medicine at the wrong time can even cause harm. My colleagues and I wondered whether midazolam, the most common sedative(镇静剂) used in surgical procedures worldwide, might interfere with the internal clock that protects the heart at night. Currently, there are no guidelines regarding when midazolam should be administered.

More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases. I believe taking drug timing into account could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide.

title: 2025年12月真题·第1套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser(理发师) about retirement plans. The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.

Both scenarios(情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s. Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.

In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.
"Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you're doing," Abraham says.

The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.

Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men. He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. They're also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.
Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.

C) 张冠李戴
C 项 More men than women are likely to stay in the labor force until their late
seventies 涉及性别差异，原文虽然第 6 段提到 particularly for men，但那是讲孤独
感、不是 general trend 数据；本段从未做性别对比。
D) ✓ 正确
The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly
20%
↔ The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement
预判出 "学历越高，延迟退休比例越高"，D 项 The higher their educational level, the
more likely they are to delay retirement 正是这一规律的语句化，无遗漏无超纲。

questions.stem: What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement according to an economist?
questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题）
【判型】题干 What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement 询问
原文中经济学家明确给出的主因，按细节题处理即可。
【拆句】主干 What is the chief reason，介词短语 for college-educated workers delaying
retirement 作后置定语，分词 delaying 修饰 workers 表正在延迟；末尾 according to an
economist 是插入限定信息源，结构清晰。
【定位】He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more
for social benefits than for financial reasons.
他指出，许多受过大学教育的劳动者选择继续留在劳动力市场，更多是出于社交方面的好
处，而不是经济原因。
【选项】A) 与原文相反
A 项 Enjoying financial security 把主因说成 "享受经济保障"，但原文明确 more for
social benefits than for financial reasons —— financial 恰恰是被否定的次要原因，
A 项正好反向。
B) ✓ 正确
more for social benefits than for financial reasons ↔ Staying connected socially
预判抓 social benefits，B 项 Staying connected socially 正面命中；其余选项均与
social 无直接对应，可一眼锁定。
C) 过度推断
C 项 Contributing more professionally 说 "在专业上贡献更多"，原文 in professional
occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more 只说他们多从事专业职业、
并享受工作，并未提 "为了贡献更多" 才不退休。
D) 无中生有
D 项 Increasing social security payments 把 social 与 financial 拼成 "提高社会保障
金"，是基于熟词 social 的乱凑，原文从未提及社会保障金（social security 是美国福利
专名）。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about people doing manual work?

options.label: A
options.text: They are eager to enjoy life after retiring.

options.label: B
options.text: They are likely to have financial troubles.

options.label: C
options.text: They generally don't enjoy doing it.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题）
【判型】题干 What does the passage say about people doing manual work 直接问原文对该群
体的具体说法，按细节题处理。
【拆句】主干 What does the passage say about ...，about 引出对象；现在分词短语 doing
manual work 后置修饰 people，相当于 who do manual work，无从句无难点。
【定位】Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring,
Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.
另一方面，从事体力劳动较多的工人则可能更期待退休；Baily 说，那些继续留下来的多半
是出于经济原因。
【选项】A) 过度推断
A 项 They are eager to enjoy life after retiring 把原文 "期待退休" 引申到 "渴望享受
退休后的生活"，原文只说期待退休、未提退休后做什么，引申了一步。
B) 过度推断
B 项 They are likely to have financial troubles 把原文 those who stay on are more
likely doing so for financial reasons 推到 "会陷入经济困境"，但 for financial
reasons 只说 "出于经济原因"，不等同于 financial troubles。
C) 无中生有
C 项 They generally don't enjoy doing it 说 "他们通常不喜欢做这工作"，但原文只
说他们更期待退休、并未直接评价是否喜欢工作；不能由 "期待退休" 直接等同 "不喜欢
工作"。
D) ✓ 正确
may be more likely to look forward to retiring ↔ They tend to anticipate retirement
预判抓 "期待退休"，D 项 They tend to anticipate retirement 是 look forward to
retiring 的标准英英同义替换，选定无误。

title: 2025年06月真题·第3套 · 选词填空

paragraphs.text: The human brain has the ability to constantly form new networks and connections between brain cells. This means the brain has an almost magical ability to change. This characteristic is  [26]  apparent in a new study, focusing on people who underwent a hemispherectomy, a surgical procedure in which half of the brain is removed to treat illness.

The findings showed that, despite missing half of this critical  [27]  , participants could function well. This was because the  [28]  half of their brain strengthened. In fact, researchers found that connections and thus communication—between parts of different brain networks are actually stronger in people who had hemispherectomies than in people with intact brains. This  [29]  that the brain is able to compensate for loss of certain brain structure.

There are many other cases in the medical  [30]  that document the brain's amazing ability to  [31]  For example, a young boy had a significant portion of his brain removed for medical reasons, which included the part of the brain  [32]  for sight. But a few years after his surgery, scientists found that he could  [33]  see. They determined that this was because other parts of his brain took over the missing part's  [34]  tasks. Another study involved people who could smell, despite missing the region in the brain that processes information about smells. Though they are not sure how these individuals  [35]  the ability to smell, scientists believe it is possible that another part of the brain took on that task.

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】G) particularly
副词
【词性槽】is __ apparent 系表结构里修饰形容词
【依据】‘尤其明显’才与下文的研究举例语气一致
This characteristic is __(26)__ apparent in a new study接的是一项新研究做例证，常见说
法是‘这一特性在……中尤为明显’；particularly apparent 是固定的强调搭配。
【竞争词】B) hardly hardly 是否定副词，与全段‘强调可塑性’相反
hardly apparent 意为‘几乎不明显’，会把全篇‘大脑可塑性惊人’的论点一下子否掉，逻辑上正话
反说。
K) still still 此处会变成‘仍然明显’，弱化强调
still apparent 表‘照旧明显’，没问题但语气平淡；本句要的是‘举新研究来凸显’的强调感，比
particularly 弱；且 still 在第 33 题‘he could __ see’里有更强的搭配需求（hardly/still see 的
二选一）。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】F) organ
名词
【词性槽】this+形容词+__ 空缺名词中心词
【依据】‘大脑’本身就是 critical organ（关键器官）
上文反复在讲 brain（大脑），代词 this 回指 brain，而大脑正是人体最关键的器官之一，
missing half of this critical __(27)__填 organ 后语义自洽：缺失了这个关键器官的一半。
【竞争词】E) literature literature 指文献，不能被‘半个’切
literature 是抽象名词‘文献/文学’，跟 half of this critical 搭不上——不能说‘缺了关键文献的一
半’；它真正的用武之地在第 30 题‘medical literature 医学文献’那种搭配里。
L) strategy strategy 指策略，与 brain 的指代对不上
this 在语篇里回指上文提到的实体，而上文核心实体是 brain（一个具体器官），不是某种策
略；且 missing half of a strategy 也不是地道说法。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】H) remaining
形容词
【词性槽】the+__+half 中间缺修饰名词的形容词
【依据】切了一半 → 强壮起来的是‘剩下的’那一半
上一题刚说 missing half of this critical organ（缺了一半），那么能 strengthened 的当
然是‘另一半，剩下的’，the __(28)__ half of their brain strengthened填 remaining 与上
文形成‘缺一半—剩一半补偿’的呼应。
【竞争词】I) responsible responsible 不能直接作前置定语修饰 half
responsible 表‘负有责任的’，习惯用法是 be responsible for…，几乎不直接前置修饰像 half 这
种抽象量词；语义上也与‘剩下的那一半’对不上。
O) visual ‘视觉的一半大脑’语义无所指
visual 是‘视觉的’，本段并未把话题缩到视觉脑区，下文谈视觉补偿是在第三段男孩例子里；放
在此处会把全段主旨从‘整体半脑代偿’偏到‘视觉’上。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】C) indicates
动词
【词性槽】This __ that… 主语+谓语+宾语从句缺谓语
【依据】‘上文现象→表明这一推论’，indicates 最中性贴切
This __(29)__ that the brain is able to compensate for loss of certain brain structure
是用上文‘连接更强’的事实推出‘大脑能代偿’这一结论，indicates that…（表明/说明……）是
英语里把现象引向结论的最标准说法。
【竞争词】N) underlines underlines 偏‘强调/凸显已成共识的事’，本句是‘推论’不是‘强调旧识’
underline that 也能接从句，但语气是‘再次强调’，前提是该结论早已被反复说过；本句是基于
上文新证据‘得出’结论，用 indicates（表明/暗示）更合逻辑流，且 underlines 偏文体强烈。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— underlines 与 indicates 都能接 that 从句、词性时态全过
关。This __(29)__ that the brain is able to compensate for loss of certain brain
structure里，主体考生一看 underlines that 也通就容易选错；防坑要看上文是‘新发现’还
是‘旧结论’，本句是新发现支撑推论，用 indicates 才对。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】E) literature
名词
【词性槽】in the medical __ 介词+形容词后的名词槽
【依据】medical literature 是固定搭配‘医学文献’
There are many other cases in the medical __(30)__ that document the brain's
amazing ability意为‘医学文献里有很多其他案例记录了大脑的惊人能力’，medical
literature（医学文献）是英语里讲学术案例来源的标准搭配。
【竞争词】L) strategy medical strategy 是‘医疗策略’，与 cases that document 对不上
strategy 指策略/方略，而本句 cases that document（记录案例的）只能存在于文献/记录里，
不能存在于‘策略’里；逻辑上 in the medical strategy 也偏怪。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】A) adapt
动词
【词性槽】ability to __ 不定式 to 后接动词原形
【依据】全篇主旨就是‘大脑能适应/代偿’
回到 overview：the brain is able to compensate for loss of certain brain structure
——‘代偿’与‘适应’语义同向；the brain's amazing ability to __(31)__填 adapt，意即‘大脑
惊人的适应能力’，与全篇主旨完全对齐。
【竞争词】D) insist insist 表‘坚持主张’，主语是大脑不通
insist 多用于人的‘坚持要求/坚持认为’，跟无生命的 brain 搭配语义怪异；且与下文举的两个例
子（视觉代偿、嗅觉代偿）无关，例证是用来证明‘适应/代偿’而非‘坚持’。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】I) responsible
形容词
【词性槽】the part of the brain __ for sight 缺后置定语形容词
【依据】固定搭配 be responsible for 锁死
看见 __ for 这种‘形容词+for’框架，几乎立刻想到 responsible for（负责……的）；the
part of the brain __(32)__ for sight即‘负责视觉的那部分大脑’，是英语里讲脑区功能的标
准说法。
【竞争词】O) visual visual 不与 for 搭配，且会和 sight 语义打架
visual 是‘视觉的’，没有 visual for… 的搭配；同时 visual 本身就含‘视觉’的意思，再加 for sight
就成了‘视觉的为了视力’，重复又不通。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】K) still
副词
【词性槽】could __ see 情态动词与原形动词之间缺副词
【依据】“切了视觉脑区还是能看见”才呼应代偿主旨
a young boy had a significant portion of his brain removed for medical reasons,
which included the part of the brain __(32)__ for sight. But a few years after his
surgery, scientists found that he could __(33)__ see.——But+几年后+发现他能看见，
要的是‘竟然还能看见’这种转折后肯定，still see 正合此意，且呼应主旨‘大脑代偿’。
【竞争词】B) hardly hardly see 是‘几乎看不见’，与 But… 转折后的肯定语气反向
hardly 是半否定副词，会把句意变成‘他几乎看不见’，那就和第三段‘大脑居然能代偿’的全段定调
彻底相反。看到 But + scientists found 的‘惊喜发现’语气，要的就是肯定的‘still’。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— hardly 是‘最熟脸’副词，最容易误填进 could __ see。he
could __(33)__ see里 could hardly see 读着也通顺，但忽视了上文 But+几年后
+scientists found 的‘惊喜发现’语气；防坑：见 But 引出的肯定发现，副词槽几乎必选肯定
型（still/even），半否定（hardly/scarcely）几乎一律错。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】O) visual
形容词
【词性槽】the missing part's __ tasks 缺修饰 tasks 的形容词
【依据】上文是‘负责视觉的脑区’，被接管的自然是视觉任务
32 题已说 the part of the brain responsible for sight，34 题接 the missing part's __
tasks——既然 missing part 负责的是 sight，那它的 tasks 就是 visual tasks（视觉任
务），语义闭环。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】J) retained
动词
【词性槽】how these individuals __ the ability 从句缺谓语动词
【依据】‘没了脑区却仍保有嗅觉能力’，retained 精准对位
people who could smell, despite missing the region in the brain that processes
information about smells. Though they are not sure how these individuals __(35)__
the ability to smell——despite missing… 与 retained the ability（保留了能力）形成完
美让步对照：脑区缺了，能力还在‘保留着’，正是‘代偿’的典型描述。
【竞争词】M) transformed transformed 是‘改造/转变’，跟 the ability to smell 搭配不通
transform 通常表‘把 A 改造为 B（transform A into B）’，跟‘嗅觉能力’搭配会变成‘改造嗅觉能
力’，与上下文‘他们居然还能闻得到’的‘保留’语义反向。

title: 2025年06月真题·第3套 · 长篇匹配（"Phantom" Traffic Jams A）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Traffic jams are a common problem of most big cities, either in developed or in developing countries, but one kind of traffic jams in particular can be especially frustrating. These are generally known as "phantom" traffic jams, in which dense traffic crawls to a halt for no apparent reason at all.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: "When caught in such a traffic jam, it is common for drivers to assume that there must be an accident, or construction or something," said Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) computer science professor Berthold Horn. "And then you drive and drive and drive… and there isn't anything there."

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The exact cause of these phantom traffic jams has long remained a mystery. But now, new research has found the cause and researchers may have come up with a solution for this frustrating traffic pattern: maintaining equal spacing between cars on the road, rather than driving so closely behind another vehicle that a collision(碰撞) is likely if that vehicle brakes suddenly.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Horn said phantom traffic jams are an emergent property of the flow of vehicles down a highway. A phantom jam begins when a car in dense traffic slows down even slightly, which causes the car behind that vehicle to slow even more—and the slowing action spreads backward through the lane of traffic like a wave, getting worse the farther it spreads. Eventually, the cars far behind are forced to stop completely or risk hitting the slower vehicles ahead—and so the traffic grinds to a halt over nothing, Horn said.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Horn has been working on the problem of phantom traffic jams for years, and he has come up with a solution: By splitting the difference between the cars in front and the cars behind, the spacing of cars in a stream of traffic can act as a damper(抑制) on phantom traffic jams. That is, it can prevent the slow-down effect from being amplified(增强) by the cars that follow behind, he said. In essence, each driver would constantly make adjustments to keep their car roughly halfway between the car in front and the car behind.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Horn calls this method of vehicle spacing bilateral(双边的) control, and he said it could be achieved with relatively simple modifications to the adaptive cruise control that many new cars already have. Adaptive cruise control is a driver assistance technology that sets a maximum speed for vehicles and automatically slows the speed of the car when traffic is sensed in front of the vehicle. The technology is also known as autonomous cruise control. Such modifications, Horn said, could help fight phantom jams within a few years, maybe decades before an alternative solution, such as networked self-driving cars, becomes a reality on the roads.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Traffic jams are caused by a number of factors, such as roads that are poorly designed or over-capacity, localized factors like city traffic-lighting patterns, and events like accidents and construction. But phantom traffic jams can make all those problems worse, Horn said. And the researchers in the new study have calculated that solving phantom jams could save at least some of the estimated $121 billion per year that traffic jams are estimated to cost the U.S. economy, Horn told Live Science.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: New research by Horn and MIT postdoctoral associate Liang Wang, published in the journal IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, shows how bilateral control can fight the problem. The researchers made computer models of real-world traffic conditions, showing how a typical U.S. freeway could benefit from cars using bilateral control. That would be in place when human drivers fail to slow down, thus avoiding tailgating(紧跟) the car in front, Horn said. "Under reasonable conditions today, you might get 1,800 cars per lane per hour throughput (the volume of traffic passing through)," he added. "But with bilateral control, you could almost double that."

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: The main alternative to increasing traffic throughput per lane has been to build more lanes and more highways, and putting in new roads is very expensive, he said. "If we can increase the throughput on major highways, even if it's only by 50 percent, that would be a big deal," Horn said.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: With the help of engineering students at high schools in Maine, Horn and Wang have also built a robot simulation(模拟) that shows how bilateral control can suppress phantom traffic jams. Increasing the spacing of vehicles dampens the effect of slowdowns by cars in front of a given car, so that the slowing is not worsened until it becomes a phantom jam, the researchers said.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: A video from the project shows a train of autonomous robots running along a track without bilateral control; they eventually back up in phantom jams. But when the robots are switched over to bilateral control (by flashing the lights in the room), each autonomous robot tries to keep itself halfway between the robot in front and the one behind; the phantom jams disappear as a result, Horn said.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Since starting his research on phantom traffic jams, Horn has learned that schools of fish and flocks of birds and bats use similar spacing strategies to avoid hitting each other while swimming or flying in densely packed groups. In particular, studies of millions of bats emerging at dusk from caves in Southeast Asia showed that each bat used a form of bilateral control to reduce the likelihood of collisions with other bats in the densely packed swarm(一大群), Horn said.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Unlike bats, birds and fish, however, humans have difficulty judging distances behind them. To address that weakness, Horn is now working with the car company Toyota to enable a form of bilateral control via modifications to existing adaptive cruise control systems, which use forward-facing sensors to judge the distance to the vehicle ahead. The bilateral control approach would include adding rear-facing sensors to determine the distance to the vehicle following a car.

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: But until those systems become standard, human drivers can help reduce phantom traffic jams simply by not following the car in front so closely. As Horn argues, "There's absolutely no advantage of tailgating the car in front of you."

title: 2025年06月真题·第3套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner table near you, but do they deserve a spot on your plate? If you tried a vegetable burger years ago and dismissed it as rubbery and flavorless, it's a good time to give meatless meat another chance. Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat. Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge.

Plant-based meats are no longer just for vegetarians. Companies such as Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat—the current superstars of the alternative protein sector—are pursuing consumers who enjoy meat but want to reduce their meat consumption for animal rights, health, or environmental reasons. So far, it's a winning strategy: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat.

Many vegetarians don't actually care for food that resembles meat. When reporter Joan Solsman, a longtime vegetarian, tried a dish from Impossible Foods, she felt so sick that she couldn't finish it. "Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn't stand to take another bite," she wrote.
Meatless meats are generally a healthier choice than beef because they are cholesterol-free, plus they're a good source of vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber.

If meatless meat can help you stick to a plant-based diet, that in itself can lead to better health. Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.
However, just because it's plant-based doesn't mean it's health food. Most imitation meats are highly processed and contain high amounts of sodium(钠) compared to traditional beef.

These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don't forget about whole grains and vegetables. Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute. They're nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today.

questions.stem: What can we expect of plant-based meats?

options.label: A
options.text: An increasing interest in their analyses.

options.label: B
options.text: An enormous effort in their promotion.

options.label: C
options.text: A huge boost in their consumption.

options.label: D
options.text: A noticeable surge in their varieties.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】What can we expect of plant-based meats? 没有出现 infer/imply/suggest，问的是一
个文中已表述的预期结果，属于事实细节题。
【拆句】What can we expect of plant-based meats? 结构是 expect sth of sb/sth（对……抱有什
么期待/预期），of 后接被期待的对象。考生熟悉的 expect sth from sb 在此处换成 of，
含义相近，不必紧张。
【定位】Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts
the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge.
分析师们不预期植物肉浪潮短期内会放缓；一份 2021 年的报告预测，到 2030 年该市场将
猛增至 740 亿美元——增幅高达 957%。
【选项】A) 偷换概念
An increasing interest in their analyses 把原文里「分析师们的预期」偷换成「对它们
分析的兴趣增长」，文章并未说人们对植物肉的分析研究兴趣上升。
B) 无中生有
An enormous effort in their promotion 谈的是「推广上的巨大努力」，原文只说市
场规模会增长，没提企业或政府投入推广，属无中生有。
C) ✓ 正确
the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge ↔
A huge boost in their consumption
预判要的是「消费规模大增」，A huge boost in their consumption 正是这个语义，
锁定 C。
D) 偷换概念
A noticeable surge in their varieties 把 surge 的对象从原文的「市场规模」换成「种
类」，原文仅提到 Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat，说
新品种已出现，但没说种类会激增。

questions.stem: What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products?

options.label: C
options.text: Most of them refrain from eating meat for health reasons.

options.label: D
options.text: Most of them eat meatless meat to protect the environment.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题）
【判型】What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods
products? 是 learn about + 名词结构，问关于该人群在原文中已写明的属性。
【拆句】What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods
products? 主干 What do we learn about consumers，buying ... 是后置的现在分词短语
作 consumers 的定语，相当于 who buy ...，结构无陷阱。
【定位】More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products
also eat meat.
在购买 Beyond Burger 和 Impossible Foods 产品的消费者中，有超过十分之九的人同时
也吃肉。
【选项】A) ✓ 正确
More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products
also eat meat
↔ They are mostly non-vegetarians
预判说的「多数也吃肉」正对应「多数非素食者」，A 命中。
B) 以偏概全
They are mostly animal-rights advocates 把动物权利说成消费者的主要身份，但原文
animal rights, health, or environmental reasons 是并列的三类动机之一，没有说大多
数是动物权利倡导者。
C) 以偏概全
Most of them refrain from eating meat for health reasons 同样把并列三动机里的
「健康」拎出来说大多数，且 refrain from eating meat（克制吃肉）与原文 reduce
their meat consumption 程度被夸大。
D) 以偏概全
Most of them eat meatless meat to protect the environment 同样犯「三选一拎为
主因」的错误，无原文比例支撑。

questions.stem: What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark?

options.label: A
options.text: They more often appeal to meat-eaters.

options.label: B
options.text: They very much resemble animal meat.

options.label: C
options.text: Some have become its signature dishes.

options.label: D
options.text: Most of them are sold as true fake meat.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （推断题）
【判型】What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's
remark? 中 conclude from ... remark 表示要从她的话里推出关于产品的判断。
【拆句】What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's
remark? 主干 What can we conclude about X from Y，about 引出推断对象（产品），
from 引出推断依据（她的话）；这是固定结构。
【定位】Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I
couldn't stand to take another bite.
或许 Impossible Foods 成功破解「逼真假肉」密码的最有力信号，就是连我（这个素食
者）都没法再吃一口。
【选项】A) 答非所问
题目要求从她的话推断 Impossible Foods 的「产品本身」特性，They more often
appeal to meat-eaters 说的是「产品更受肉食者欢迎」，那是 Q52 答案，不是 Q53
的推断方向。
B) ✓ 正确
Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat ↔
They very much resemble animal meat
预判要的是「产品逼真像真肉」，They very much resemble animal meat 直接对应，
锁 B。
C) 无中生有
Some have become its signature dishes 说这些菜成了「招牌菜」，原文只说她试吃
了 a dish from Impossible Foods，并未说哪些是招牌。
D) 偷换概念
Most of them are sold as true fake meat 把 realistic fake meat（逼真的假肉）改成
sold as true fake meat（作为「真假肉」出售），不仅商业化（销售行为）是原文没有
的，true 修饰 fake meat 的逻辑也与「产品像真肉」相违。

questions.stem: Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health?

options.label: A
options.text: It frees people from any known link to cancer.

options.label: B
options.text: It provides all the nutrients for staying healthy.

options.label: C
options.text: It helps maintain normal blood pressure and blood sugar.

options.label: D
options.text: It reduces various health risks posed by meat consumption.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题）
【判型】Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health? 用 Why 提问，
原文有明确因果链时仍属细节题。
【拆句】Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health? 中主语是 the
habit of doing sth（做某事的习惯）这个抽象名词短语，谓语 lead to 表示导致，结构平
铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat
have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.
不仅红肉被发现与癌症相关，研究还显示放弃吃肉的人血压更低、平均血糖更低、胆固醇水
平也更低。
【选项】A) 过度推断
It frees people from any known link to cancer 中 frees ... from any known link 表
示「完全免除任何已知关联」，但原文只说红肉与癌症「被发现相关」（red meat
been linked to cancer），并未说弃肉就能彻底斩断所有癌症关联。
B) 过度推断
It provides all the nutrients for staying healthy 说植物饮食提供「所有保持健康所需
的营养」，P4 只列了维生素、矿物质、蛋白质、纤维四项，没说「全部」。
C) 以偏概全
It helps maintain normal blood pressure and blood sugar 只提血压和血糖，漏了胆
固醇和癌症，且 maintain normal 意为「维持正常」，比 lower 表达的「降低」程度
还弱。
D) ✓ 正确
Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have
lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.
↔ It reduces various health risks posed by meat consumption
预判要「综合性下降」，D 的 various health risks 正好覆盖了四种风险，是唯一概
括项。

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】J) referred
动词
【词性槽】Famously ___ to as 是过去分词作状语
【依据】be referred to as 是"被称为"的固定搭配
Famously __(26)__ to as 'The Master of Suspense' 中 to as 紧贴空后，这是经典短语
refer to A as B = 把 A 称作 B 的被动式 be referred to as = 被称为。代入即 "以"悬疑
大师"之名广为人知"，与后文 one of the most influential filmmakers 的赞誉口吻完全
一致。
【竞争词】A) caught 搭配不成立
catch 不和 to as 搭配；caught to as 在英语里不存在这个固定结构。
I) punished 语义反

K) stood 搭配不通

合适。
M) tuned 义不沾边
tune 表"调音/调频"，和"被称为"风马牛不相及，也不与 to as 搭配。
O) worshipped 搭配错位

in the history of cinema = 电影史上最有影响力的导演之一，是地道表达。
【竞争词】F) incentive 义不沾边

title: 2025年06月真题·第2套 · 长篇匹配（Is juicing actually good）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item—especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients. Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy. All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable. The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: But is juicing really as healthy as we think? Most foods containing fructose—a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices—don't seem to have harmful effects as long as they're not contributing to excess daily calories. This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit's cells. It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: But this is not the case with fruit juice. Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed. This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as 'free sugars'—which also include honey and the sugars added to foods. It's recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day. The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice's fructose is absorbed more quickly. Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin(胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level. Over time, this mechanism can wear out, increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes. Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years. The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit—but they still lack valuable fibre. Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it's recommended adults consume 30g per day.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories. In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto's Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health—including risk of diabetes and heart disease—were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet. He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars. His aim? To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice. However, when the calories weren't in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit—and even fruit juice. Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable. The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don't lead to over-consumption of calories. But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it's part of a diet that has more calories overall, it's less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren't overweight. But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research. Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn't make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in. And extra calories can contribute to weight gain. One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical(药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Another reason for fruit juice's recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body. However, "the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false," says Clemens. "We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: And juice isn't a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either. "There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them," says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine. "You end up with sugary water with some vitamins."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Plus, she adds, it's not an ideal way to reach the advised 'five a day'. "People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don't realise this isn't just about getting vitamins," she says. "It's also about reducing the amount of grain carbs(碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre." So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits. It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake. It provides us with vitamins—but fruit juice is far from a quick fix.

title: 2025年06月真题·第2套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: We all take a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions. But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes. Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives.

We hear sayings like "dress for the job you want; not the job you have". Most people don't really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings. Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing.

We consider some clothes to be powerful, some to be fun, and so on. We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes. We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel. This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior.

There's a reason tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'. It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business. Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers.

While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn't a great idea when we want to socialize. Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes.

On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday; since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week. I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits?

paragraphs.text: With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.

The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic(交响乐的) orchestras have had on society's taste in music.

A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.

Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.

Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.

While we know that adults use a large variety of attributes to manage and create impressions, we don't yet know whether children  [32]  and use the fact that different attributes are valuable at different times to different  [33]  . It's important for us to further consider where in this process children succeed in controlling their reputation and where they  [34]  .

title: 2025年06月真题·第1套 · 长篇匹配（Getting young minds into）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Recently, a leading design federation in the UK warned that the UK could face a creative skills shortage, after the latest figures revealed a drop of almost 10 percent in students studying Design and Technology. These figures showed that the number of pupils that sat exams in Design and Technology fell 10 percent from 204,788 to 185,279 last year.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Chief executive John Kampfner of the Creative Industries Federation thinks that this drop in figures has worrying implications for the skills pipeline in Britain's hugely successful arts and creative industries. He said, "We already have skills shortages in many jobs such as animation(动画制作) and special effects." He added: "Engineering, which requires a similar mix of creative and technical skills, also has recruitment problems."

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Many other designers and architects have expressed concern over the future supply of home-grown talent for UK firms, and industry bodies have pointed out that there has been a lack of roots-level support. However, if these designers had visited the Design Museum shop in London earlier this year their fears may have been eased. With £10 to spend, they could have bought a fascinating children's toy called "Dazzle Racer". An automotive cylinder(圆柱体), it included a wind-up, elastic(有弹性的)-band-powered mechanism, minimal parts, all 100 percent recycled, and lots of stickers. It was good fun, simple, eye-catching and very original.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Well, you'd expect the Design Museum to commission and make some interesting items, but this one was different. Designed by a group of six Year 9 and Year 10 boys from Finchley Catholic High School, the toy was the winning entry in the museum's 2015 Design Ventura competition, which brings the business of design to life for students aged 13 to 16 by challenging them to develop a new creative, sustainable and commercially feasible product for the Design Museum shop and attracts hundreds of entries nationwide.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "We did Design Ventura in my previous school," says Liam Hourican, Finchley Catholic High School's design technology curriculum leader. "Then when I changed schools four years ago, I introduced it here because it helps to develop so many skills."

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The theme for last year's competition was "Move", and Hourican began with three groups working in lunch breaks and after school before selecting the group with the most innovative idea. Each participating school may submit just one proposal. "It's the taking part and doing the work which is important," he says. "And I never dreamt we'd win."

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Catherine Ritman Smith, head of learning at the Design Museum, is expecting around 10,000 participants aged 13 to 16 to take part this year and says that the project—funded by Deutsche Bank as part of its youth engagement programme Born To Be—is the biggest event in the museum's calendar. "We started Design Ventura with around 800 young people in 2010 and it has grown steadily since," she says. "Teachers like it because the skills are all transferable and it helps to validate the value of design as a subject," she explains, telling me that nearly 600 schools have taken part so far.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: So how does the competition work? A single-word theme is announced in the summer. This year it is "Change". Schools work with groups to produce imaginative design ideas for a product in simple materials that could sell for £10 in the Design Museum shop. Participating schools then register by November and eventually submit their design idea. Along the way there is training and support for teachers and tutoring for students from designers. An additional bonus is when the winners see their design on sale in the spring of the following year.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Hourican and his pupils have happy memories of spending a whole day at the museum, having been selected as one of 10 shortlisted schools to present their idea to a panel of judges, including designer Jasper Conran. Then they worked with the Kin Design Studio in Shoreditch, met designers at their school and attended a lunch with Deutsche Bank employees. The students helped to make decisions and there were plenty of discussions—they changed the product's name, for example.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: "One of the really useful things about this competition," says Hourican, "is that there's a commercial element because the product is going on sale for real and the boys had to learn about budgeting and marketing, as well as designing their game." Profits go to charity. "The winning team chooses where it wants the profits to go," says Ritman Smith. "The Finchley Catholic High School product raised about £1,000 for Great Ormond Street Hospital." Winning entries in past years have included a make-your-own cloth kit called Dove Bunting and a threefold, wallet-sized travel game with goals at each end, called Badoiiing.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: It costs the schools nothing to participate in Design Ventura; the professional designers provide their services for free. Among them are architect Asif Khan, a Design Museum trustee who has worked as designer-in-residence at the museum, helping emerging architects. He has recently been commissioned to design the new Museum of London building in Smithfield.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Another is television presenter and interior designer Naomi Cleaver, who is one of the competition's judges. "I'm very keen to encourage young people," she says, observing that design brings together other subjects such as literature, art, history, geography and science. "Now that design education is limited in the curriculum, I'm all in favour of competitions such as Design Ventura, which helps to bring the standard curriculum to life," says Cleaver. "And the judging day is terrific fun. Some of these students are very imaginative. One group presented their idea in the form of a puppet show and we see some marvelous demonstration models. I'm always impressed by the levels of confidence and the support the students get from their teachers."

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Ritman Smith adds: "Design technology has become a tricky subject to make a case for, and we've heard of departments closing in some schools. We find that if pupils take part in Design Ventura in Year Nine it can be the trigger which leads them to opt for it at General Certificate of Secondary Education, so we are helping to keep alive something which is crucial to industry and entrepreneurship."

paragraphs.text: New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. Experts say too much happiness can stop the bears from searching for new mates.

Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival by "reducing or fragmenting their natural: habitats", The Times reported. But the new research suggests that a "modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation" may actually help preserve panda populations.

The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity.

For their study—outlined in a paper in the journal Conservation Biology—the team looked at genetic diversity and spread among a Chinese panda population. The ideal level of perfectly livable habitat was found to be only 80% of an area, with the remainder either too harsh or too affected by human activity.
The experts concluded that pandas should ideally "be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates".

Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering.
Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.

"Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes," said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. "It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence."
The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.
