法，无 infer/imply 字样。
【拆句】题干 What does the author say about the ability to be persuasive in the first
paragraph? 主干为 What does the author say about X，X 是 the ability to be
persuasive；in the first paragraph 是地点状语修饰 say。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。
【定位】For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes
naturally. For the rest of us, persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time.
对我们中的一些人来说，说服是与生俱来的天赋，影响他人的能力是天生的；对我们其余的
人来说，说服技巧是可以随时间学习并培养的。
【选项】A) ✓ 正确
For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality ↔ born with it
persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time ↔ be able to cultivate it
预判要求“天生或后天习得”两端都覆盖，仅 People may either be born with it or be
able to cultivate it 用 either...or 句式完整对应两端。
B) 答非所问
It proves crucial in making others follow one's course of action 把首段对“能力来
源”的说明换成了“能力的重要性”，回答的不是 What does the author say 这个角度的
问题。
C) 以偏概全
It refers to the natural and instinctive power of influencing one's coworkers 只截
取了“天生本能”那一半（some of us），漏掉了“后天习得”那一半（the rest of us），
且把场景窄化到 coworkers。
D) 无中生有
People may view it as both a means to convince others and an art of
communication 中的 art of communication 在首段并未提及，原文只说 the art of
persuasion，把 persuasion 偷换成 communication。
questions.locateHint: For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes

questions.stem: Why are persuasion skills greatly valued in the workplace?

options.label: A
options.text: They enable employees to be convinced of their long-term gains.

options.label: B
options.text: They enable employees to trust their leaders unconditionally.

options.label: C
options.text: They help motivate coworkers to strive for a common goal.

options.label: D
options.text: They help an organization to broaden its vision effectively.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】Why are persuasion skills greatly valued in the workplace? 问的是被广泛重视的具体原
因，是文中可直接读出的事实，不要求跨段综合推断。
【拆句】题干 Why are persuasion skills greatly valued in the workplace? 是 Why + be + 过去
分词 valued 构成的被动疑问句，主语是 persuasion skills；in the workplace 是地点状
语。被动语态把动作发出方（雇主）省略了，考生需要意识到“被谁所重视”的隐含主语在原
文是 employers。
【定位】Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your
ideas, it'll also help you motivate them to achieve a common goal.
有效运用说服技巧不仅有助于让你的同事对你的想法感到兴奋，也有助于你激励他们为实现
共同目标而努力。
【选项】A) 无中生有
They enable employees to be convinced of their long-term gains 中的 long-term
gains 在原文找不到对应，原文 long-term mission 谈的是组织的长期使命，并非员工
的长远收益。
B) 过度推断
They enable employees to trust their leaders unconditionally 中 unconditionally
是绝对化表述，原文只谈“激励”，从未要求“无条件信任”，属于过度推断。
C) ✓ 正确
help you motivate them to achieve a common goal ↔
help motivate coworkers to strive for a common goal
预判“激励同事为共同目标”两要素，They help motivate coworkers to strive for a
common goal 在句法结构上几乎是原文的平移，是最贴近预判的选项。
D) 偷换概念
They help an organization to broaden its vision effectively 把原文的“让员工
committed to vision”（员工对愿景的认同）偷换成“拓展组织的愿景”（broaden its
vision），动作和受体都被换掉。
questions.locateHint: Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your

questions.stem: What should people do to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace?

options.label: B
options.text: Avoid getting involved in conflicts with others.

options.label: C
options.text: Understand the reason for pursuing their goals.

options.label: D
options.text: Commit themselves fully to their ideas and plans.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题）
【判型】What should people do to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace? 提问“为达成
X 该做什么”，答案是原文中显性陈述的前置条件，无需推断。
【拆句】题干 What should people do to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace? 主干是
What should people do，to learn... at the workplace 是不定式做目的状语。考生易把
to learn 误读为定语修饰 do，正确理解应是“为了学会...，人们该做什么”。
【定位】Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just
as important.
良好的沟通是有效说服的第一步，但逻辑和推理同样重要。
【选项】A) ✓ 正确
Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion ↔
Acquire effective communication skills
预判要求“先做好沟通”，Acquire effective communication skills 用 acquire 动作动词
直译 first step 隐含的“获取动作”，匹配度最高。
B) 偷换概念
Avoid getting involved in conflicts with others 把原文 how to handle conflicts（处
理冲突）偷换成 avoid... conflicts（回避冲突），原文从未让人避开冲突。
C) 张冠李戴
Understand the reason for pursuing their goals 把原文中的“帮别人理解为什么要追
求该目标”张冠到“自己理解”，主语错位。
D) 答非所问
Commit themselves fully to their ideas and plans 描述的是听众被说服后的状态
（fully committed），是“说服成功”的结果，而题干问的是说服者该做的前置条件。
questions.locateHint: Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just

questions.stem: When are you more likely to succeed in persuading your coworkers?

options.label: A
options.text: When they are convinced you work in their interests while sacrificing your own

options.label: B
options.text: When they become aware of the potential strength of the judgements you make

options.label: C
options.text: When they become aware of the meaningful relationships you keep with them.

options.label: D
options.text: When they are convinced they will make achievements together with you.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题）
【判型】When are you more likely to succeed in persuading your coworkers? 问的是某客观条
件下的可能性，文中第四段直陈条件句，可直接定位。
【拆句】题干 When are you more likely to succeed in persuading your coworkers? 主干是
When are you more likely to succeed，to succeed in doing 是固定搭配。考生易把
more likely 误读作纯感情色彩词，应理解为“在何种条件下，更可能”，相当于在问触发
条件。
【定位】Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you.
当你的同事与你一起取得成功时，他们更可能同意你的看法。
【选项】A) 过度推断
while sacrificing your own 是原文从未提及的“牺牲自我利益”，原文只说“为对方利益
着想”，未要求牺牲自己。
B) 偷换概念
the potential strength of the judgements you make 把原文 they trust your
judgement and strength 中的并列两件事偷换成“判断的潜在力量”，concept 被悄悄
合并改写。
C) 答非所问
meaningful relationships you keep with them 是说服力的前提条件（说服者需要做
的事），不是同事被说服的触发条件——题干问的是后者。
D) ✓ 正确
when they succeed alongside you ↔
When they are convinced they will make achievements together with you
预判“双方共同成功才更易被说服”，they will make achievements together with you
是定位句 they succeed alongside you 的同义改写，方向一致。
questions.locateHint: Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you.

questions.stem: Why are organizations and leaders advised to adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes?

options.label: A
options.text: To convince employees of the value of collaboration

options.label: B
options.text: To allow for the preferences of most people of today

options.label: C
options.text: To improve on traditional organizational structures

options.label: D
options.text: To adapt to employees' ever-changing working styles

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题）
【判型】Why are organizations and leaders advised to adopt powerful persuasion skills to
bring about necessary changes? 问的是该建议的事实依据，文中末段直陈，无须推断。
【拆句】题干 Why are organizations and leaders advised to adopt powerful persuasion skills
to bring about necessary changes? 是 Why + 被动 are advised to do 的疑问句，to
bring about... 是不定式做目的状语。该结构隐含的动作发出方是“作者”，被建议方是
organizations and leaders；考生需识别这是在问作者给出此建议的依据。
【定位】A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational
structures; no one likes to be told what to do or to be pushed around. Therefore, organizations
and leaders should adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes.
绝大多数人更喜欢协作与团队合作，而非传统组织结构；没人喜欢被指使或被任意摆布。因
此，组织和领导者应当采用有力的说服技巧来带来必要的变革。
【选项】A) 答非所问
To convince employees of the value of collaboration 把“顺应大多数人偏好”换成了
“说服员工相信协作的价值”——原文是员工自己已经偏好协作，无需再被说服其价值。
B) ✓ 正确
A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational
structures
↔ To allow for the preferences of most people of today
题干问“为什么被建议这么做”，To allow for the preferences of most people of
today 用 To do 不定式直接给出目的-原因，是最贴合预判的答案。
C) 无中生有
To improve on traditional organizational structures 把“改善传统组织结构”列为目
的，但原文 traditional organizational structures 出现的语境是“人们更偏好协作而非
传统组织结构”，并未把“改善”它作为说服技巧的目的。
D) 无中生有
To adapt to employees' ever-changing working styles 中的 ever-changing
working styles（不断变化的工作方式）原文未提，原文谈的是“偏好”而非“工作方式的
变化”。
questions.locateHint: A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational

title: 2024年06月真题·第2套 · 选词填空

paragraphs.text: A team of researchers led by Priyanka Joshi examined the degree to which men and women relied on "communicative abstraction" to verbally convey their ideas and emotions. Communicative abstraction, according to the researchers, reflects the tendency of people to use "abstract speech that focuses on the broader picture and  [26]  purpose of action rather than concrete speech focusing on details and the means of  [27]  action." Interestingly, they found that men were far more likely to speak in the abstract than were women.

To arrive at this  [28]  , the researchers examined the linguistic(语言的) patterns of men and women in over 600,000 blog posts written on websites. To do this, the researchers computed abstractness ratings for  [29]  40,000 commonly used words in the English language. Words considered to be concrete could be easily visualized, such as "table" or "chair". Words that were more  [30]  to visualize, for example, "justice" or "morality" were considered to be more abstract. They found that men used  [31]  more abstract language in their blog posts.

What is the  [32]  of this effect? The researchers suggest that power differences between the genders—that is, men having more power in society—might be a key determinant(决定因素). For instance, in a follow-up study conducted with a sample of 300 students, the researchers  [33]  power dynamics in an interpersonal setting to see if this would influence communicative abstraction. They found that participants in a high-power interviewer role were more likely to give abstract descriptions of behaviors than were participants in a low-power interviewee role. This suggests that communicating more abstractly does not reflect a  [34]  tendency of men or women but rather  [35]  within specific contexts.

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】O) ultimate
形容词
【词性槽】and 前后并列，名词 purpose 之前需要一个与 broader 平行的形容词
【依据】ultimate purpose 是英语固定搭配，意为「最终目的」
the ultimate purpose of action「行动的最终目的」与 the broader picture「更宏观的画
面」语义共振，都指向抽象 speech 关注「全局/根本」。与 abstract speech that focuses
on the broader picture and __(26)__ purpose of action 的语境严丝合缝。
【竞争词】D) difficult difficult purpose 搭配生硬、语义跑偏
difficult 表「困难的」，「困难的行动目的」既不是固定搭配，也与「抽象 speech 关注大局」
的语义无关。留给真正讲「难以…」的空位（30 题）。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】B) attaining
动词
【词性槽】介词 of 之后需要动名词作宾语
【依据】与前句的 purpose of action 构成「目的—手段」对照
前一句讲抽象 speech 关注 the broader picture and __(26)__ purpose of action，本句讲
具体 speech 关注 details and the means of __(27)__ action。purpose of action（行动
的目的）与 means of attaining action（达成行动的手段）正好构成「为什么做—怎么
做」的对偶，attaining action 意为「实现行动」，逻辑严密。
【竞争词】K) refraining 搭配硬伤：refrain 是不及物动词，必须接 from
refrain 表「克制、避免」时，固定搭配是 refrain from doing sth.，不能直接接名词宾语
action；且语义上「克制行动的手段」与「具体讲细节」无关，逻辑也跑偏。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】C) conclusion
名词
【词性槽】指示代词 this 之后需要名词
【依据】arrive at a conclusion 是固定搭配，意为「得出结论」
上一段 they found that men were far more likely to speak in the abstract than were
women 已经摆出了研究结论；本段开头 To arrive at this __(28)__, the researchers
examined…「为得出这一结论，研究者们考察了…」，回指上段的研究发现，conclusion
是英语阅读里 arrive at 最高频的宾语之一。
【竞争词】N) source
搭配错位且语义反向：arrive at this source 不通，且 source 强调「源头」与此处「结
论」反向
arrive at a source 不是英语习惯搭配；语义上 source 指「根源/来源」，应该是「为查明这一
现象的根源」才用 source——而那正是 32 题要做的事。把 source 留给 32 题，conclusion 留
给 28 题，分工干净。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】A) approximately
副词
【词性槽】空后紧跟数词，需要修饰数词的副词
【依据】approximately 是英语里专门修饰数词表「大约」的标配副词
approximately + 数字 是英语里几乎固定的表达「大约 40,000 个常用词」，对应中文「研
究者对大约 4 万个常用英语单词计算了抽象度评分」，与 computed abstractness ratings
for __(29)__ 40,000 commonly used words 完全贴合。
【竞争词】H) legally 语义跑偏：合法地 ≠ 大约
legally 表「合法地、在法律上」，与「4 万个单词」的语境无关——研究者不是「合法地对
40,000 个单词评分」，纯粹是中文译过去也读不通的错配。
M) significantly significantly 修饰程度/动作，不修饰具体数词
significantly 表「显著地」，一般修饰动词或形容词（如 used significantly more /
significantly higher），不与具体数字 40,000 直接搭配。这一项要留给后面真正涉及「显著多/
显著高」的空。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】D) difficult
形容词
【词性槽】be 动词 were 之后作表语
【依据】与上一句「easily visualized」形成 easy ↔ difficult 的反义对照
前一句说具体词「Words considered to be concrete could be easily visualized, such as
table or chair」（容易在脑中可视化）；本句说抽象词「more difficult to visualize, for
example, justice or morality」（更难可视化）。easy ↔ difficult 的对照轴是命题人埋的
明信号。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】M) significantly
副词
【词性槽】动词 used 与比较级 more abstract language 之间需要副词修饰
【依据】significantly more 是研究/统计文体的高频搭配「显著更多」
research / statistics 文体里 significantly more / significantly higher 几乎是标配表达
「在统计上显著高于」，与 They found that men used __(31)__ more abstract
language 强调「男性使用抽象语言显著多于女性」的研究主旨完全吻合。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】N) source
名词
【词性槽】定冠词 the 之后、of 之前需要名词
【依据】the source of this effect 意为「这一效应的根源」，正是下文要追究的「为何如此」
紧接着 The researchers suggest that power differences between the genders…might
be a key determinant——把权力差异当作「关键决定因素」，正是回答「root/source 在
哪里」的问题。source「根源」与 determinant「决定因素」语义共振。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】I) manipulated
动词
【词性槽】主语 the researchers 之后需要谓语动词（过去式）
【依据】manipulate 在心理学实验语境里的固定义：操控/调控自变量
实验研究中 manipulate 是术语：研究者「人为操控/调控」某一变量看其因果效应。原文
in a follow-up study conducted with a sample of 300 students, the researchers
__(33)__ power dynamics in an interpersonal setting to see if this would influence
communicative abstraction——研究者「操控了人际情境中的权力动态」，正是典型的实
验设计描述。
【竞争词】G) ignored 逻辑反向：研究的就是 power dynamics，怎么会去「忽视」它
ignored「忽视」与本句目的「to see if this would influence…」（看它是否影响…）正相反
——研究者是要观察权力变量的作用，不可能去忽视它。
J) recommended 搭配不当：recommend「推荐」与权力动态不搭
recommend 用于「向某人推荐某物/做法」，把 power dynamics 当作被推荐物在语义上不
通，也不是实验研究术语。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 G) —— ignored 词形完全合规，靠中文直觉容易选——但因果与
下文反向。ignored 与 manipulated 都是过去式及物动词，初看「忽视权力动态」似乎也
能讲。但本句目的状语 to see if this would influence communicative abstraction 表明
研究者要观察其作用，逻辑上必须「调控/操作」它而非「忽视」它。防坑口诀：动词空务
必把目的/结果状语读完再下手。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】F) fixed
形容词
【词性槽】不定冠词 a 与名词 tendency 之间是定语位
【依据】与下半句 rather…within specific contexts 形成「固有 vs 因情境而异」的对比
原句结构 does not reflect a __ tendency…but rather __ within specific contexts 是 not
A but B 的反义对比。后半 within specific contexts（在具体情境中浮现）暗示「不是与生
俱来、不变的」，对偶位填 fixed「固定的、固有的」最贴：「不是男女固有的倾向，而是
在特定情境中浮现」。
【竞争词】D) difficult 语义不沾：困难的倾向？讲不通
difficult tendency「困难的倾向」既不符合搭配习惯，也与「不是…而是…在情境中浮现」的反
义结构不对偶。
O) ultimate
义近但方向错：ultimate 强调「终极/根本」，但本句要的是「固有不变」的对照
ultimate tendency 字面像「根本倾向」，单看半句似乎也通。但它无法与 within specific
contexts「在具体情境中」构成清晰反义；真正的对照只能是「固定不变 vs 因情境而异」，故
fixed 比 ultimate 更精准——而且 ultimate 已经在 26 题与 purpose 搭配用掉了，依「用过即
划」也不能再用。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 O) —— ultimate tendency 看着也通——其实 fixed 才与 within
specific contexts 构成反义。主体考生最常踩的坑：抓住「ultimate」的「最终的、根本
的」译义后觉得 ultimate tendency「根本倾向」也讲得通。问题是 ultimate 与紧随其后
的 but rather __(35)__ within specific contexts 构不成清晰反义，而 fixed「固定的、固有
的」恰好与「在具体情境中浮现」对偶。防坑口诀：not A but B 句式里，A 的词义必须能
从 B 反推出来。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】E) emerges
动词
【词性槽】but rather 后并列谓语，需与前句 reflect 平行的第三人称单数动词
【依据】与 within specific contexts「在具体情境中」最自然搭配——浮现、出现
emerge within/in specific contexts「在特定情境中浮现」是地道搭配，对应「这种抽象表
达倾向是因情境而生」的结论，与 does not reflect a __(34)__ fixed tendency（不是固有
倾向）正好对仗。
【竞争词】L) signals signals 是及物动词，需要宾语，不能裸接 within…
signals 作动词时意为「表明、预示」，常接宾语（如 signals a change）。这里空后直接跟介

title: 2024年06月真题·第2套 · 长篇匹配（How to better work towar）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Hal Hershfield, a psychologist at the UCLA Anderson School of Management, wanted to know why people weren't saving for retirement. Across the board, people are living longer. Logically, they'll need more money to live comfortably in their post-work years. And yet, savings rates in the U.S. have gone down in recent decades, not up.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: To help explain this seemingly irrational behavior, Hershfield and his team scanned the brains of study participants while asking them to what degree various traits(特征)—like "honorable" or "funny"—applied to their current self, their future self, a current other, or a future other. As participants answered, Hershfield's team recorded which parts of their brains lit up. Unsurprisingly, people's brains were most active when thinking about their current selves and least active when thinking about a current other. But the team found that participants' brain activity while considering their future selves more closely resembled their brain activity while thinking about a current other rather than the current self.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Put in practical terms, when thinking of yourself in a month or a year or a decade, your brain registers that person in ways similar to how it would register Taylor Swift or the mailman. Understood in that way, saving for retirement is the equivalent of giving money away to someone else entirely.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: In light of Hershfield's study, one simple question arises: Is it possible to make our present selves give a damn about our future selves? The answers are anything but simple.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Seen through the lens of the present self versus the future self, our self-defeating actions—like choosing to watch television rather than go to the gym—suddenly make perfect sense. We get to enjoy the very concrete, immediate benefits of our actions while someone else (namely, our future selves) suffers the hypothetical(假设的), far-off consequences. As a result, the decisions we make for our present selves often look very different from our decisions for our future selves. We believe that tomorrow will be different. We believe that we will be different tomorrow; but in doing so, we prioritize our current mood over the consequences of our inaction for the future self.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Understanding our procrastination(拖延) through the lens of the present and future selves, we're left with three possible solutions: The first is to force your future self to do whatever your present self doesn't want to do. The second is to convince your present self that your future self is, in fact, still you. If the central problem is that we think of our future selves as other people, it follows that trying to identify more closely with our future selves will encourage us to make better long-term decisions.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: In a follow-up study, Hershfield wanted to explore ways to bridge the disconnect between the present and future selves and encourage people to save more for retirement. He and his team took photos of study participants, and then used image processing to visually age their faces. Participants were then placed in a virtual reality setting where they could look into a mirror and see their aged selves looking back at them. Participants who saw their aged selves said they would save 30% more of their salary for retirement than the control group.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Whatever your long-term goals may be—getting in better shape, launching your own business, writing a book—thinking about your deadline in terms of days rather than months or years can help you wrap your mind around how close the future really is.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: The third solution is to forget about your future self and use your present self's love of instant gratification(满足感) to your advantage. While the two tactics(手段) above can be effective in making better long-term choices, in the end, you're still struggling against human nature. Our brains are hard-wired for instant gratification. Instead of fighting your present self's need for immediate rewards, why not use it to your advantage? When most of us set goals, we focus on long-term results we want to see—e.g., losing weight, getting a promotion, retiring in comfort, etc. While those visions of our future selves can be inspiring, when it comes to actually doing the day-to-day work, it may be more effective to reframe activities in terms of their immediate, or at least very near-term, rewards.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Take writing this article, for instance. It's easy for me to imagine how amazing it will feel at the end of the workday to have this article done. This isn't just my opinion. Research partners Kaitlin Woolley of Cornell University and Ayelet Fishbach of the University of Chicago have made a career out of studying the differences between the goals that people achieve and the ones that fall to the wayside.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: "In one study, we asked people online about the goals they set at the beginning of the year. Most people set goals to achieve delayed, long-term benefits, such as career advancement, debt repayment, or improved health. We asked these individuals how enjoyable it was to pursue their goal, as well as how important their goal was. We also asked whether they were still working on their goals two months after setting them. We found that enjoyment predicted people's goal persistence two months after setting the goal far more than how important they rated their goal to be," Woolley said.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: This pattern held true across a wide variety of goals from exercising to studying to eating healthier foods. For example, people ate 50% more of a healthy food when directed to focus on the good taste rather than the long-term health benefits. Other studies have shown a greater uptake of exercise in people who were told to think of the enjoyment of doing the exercise now rather than future health gains.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: These findings suggest that when it comes to achieving your goals, enjoying the process itself is more important than wanting the long-term benefits. In other words, present self trumps(战胜) future self. Who says instant gratification has to be a bad thing? By all means, set ambitious long-term goals for your future self, but when it comes to actually following through day-to-day, make sure your present self knows what's in it for her too.

title: 2024年06月真题·第2套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: People often wonder why some entrepreneurs have greater success than others. Is it habits, connections, luck, work ethic or any other behavior? I believe the key to success is willpower. Willpower is the ability to control yourself. It is a strong determination that allows you to do something difficult. It is a behavior we are born with more than one we learn; however, it is possible to not only learn it, but also strengthen it with constant exercise.

Willpower is just like a muscle; to keep it strong you need to constantly exercise it. People with a great amount of willpower have the discipline to develop positive, successful habits. Even with an incredible amount of talent, without the discipline and motivation to create positive habits, it can be difficult to achieve success.

Willpower and habits go hand in hand. It is critical to create good habits and take the actions necessary to stick to those habits day in and day out for greater success. Almost half of our daily actions are part of our habits and not decisions, so once the correct habits are in place, you will automatically perform those tasks on a day-to-day basis.

The best way to create and stick to a habit is to have strong motivation. It's easier to change your habits to lose weight if you have a health issue and you want to be around longer for your kids, or if your business is something you're passionate about. Having a valuable outcome associated with a habit will help you stick to that habit permanently.
The art of self-control is one that most successful individuals have mastered. Self-control enables you to avoid behaviors that don't contribute to your success and adopt those that do.

Because there is a delayed satisfaction associated with self-control, it can be easy to get off track. However, if you work on sticking to those small positive habits one day at a time, it becomes easier to stay strong and achieve that delayed reward. Once a reward is achieved, it is much easier to continue sticking to your habits.

questions.stem: How does the art of self-control help us succeed?

options.label: A
options.text: By allowing us to remain clear-headed permanently.

options.label: B
options.text: By enabling us to alter our behaviors constantly.

options.label: C
options.text: By enabling us to take positive actions

options.label: D
options.text: By allowing us to avoid taking risks.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】How does the art of self-control help us succeed? 用 how 询问机制，要求贴文给出
self-control 起作用的方式，属细节题。
【拆句】How does the art of self-control help us succeed? 主干 How does X help us (to)
succeed；help 后省略 to，接动词原形 succeed。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

those that do.
自控让你能够避开那些无助于成功的行为，并采纳那些有助于成功的行为。
【选项】A) 无中生有
原文未提"保持头脑清醒"，更未说 permanently；选项凭空生造"永远清醒"。
B) 与原文相反

C) ✓ 正确
adopt those that do ↔ By enabling us to take positive actions
Self-control enables you to ↔ By enabling us to
预判同时含"避开"与"采纳"两面，选项 By enabling us to take positive actions 抓住其
中"采纳正向行为"的一面，是定位句的合法概括（避开 negative = 接近 positive，二者
同向）。
D) 偷换概念
原文是 avoid behaviors that don't contribute to your success，避的是"无益行为"，
不是 risks；"风险"是文中从未出现的概念。

questions.stem: Why can it be difficult for us to maintain self-control?

options.label: A

【答案】B （细节题）

【选项】A) 无中生有

B) ✓ 正确

We may not get immediate rewards from self-control.

担，是 because 句的正反同义改写。

自控与痛苦绑定。

原文说 if you work on sticking to those small positive habits...it becomes easier
to...achieve that delayed reward，重点是"小习惯"带来"延迟的大回报"；small
benefits 把延迟错读成"好处本身小"。

title: 2024年06月真题·第2套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: Today, most scientific research is funded by government grants, companies doing research and development, and non-profit foundations. As a society, we reap the rewards from this science, but we also help pay for it. You indirectly support science through taxes you pay, products and services you purchase, and donations you make.

Funding for science has changed with the times. Historically, science has been largely supported through private patronage(资助), church sponsorship, or simply paying for the research yourself. Today, researchers are likely to be funded by a mix of grants from various government agencies, institutions, and foundations. Other research is funded by private companies. Such corporate sponsorship is widespread in some fields. Almost 75% of U.S. clinical trials in medicine are paid for by private companies. And, of course, some researchers today still fund small-scale studies out of their own pockets. Most of us can't afford to do nuclear research as a private hobby, but birdwatchers, rock collectors, and others can do real research on a limited budget.

In a perfect world, money wouldn't matter—all scientific studies would be completely objective. But in the real world, funding may introduce biases. Drug research sponsored by the pharmaceutical(制药的) industry is more likely to end up favoring the drug under consideration than studies sponsored by government grants or charitable organizations. Similarly, nutrition research sponsored by the food industry is more likely to end up favoring the food under consideration than independently funded research.

So what should we make of all this? Should we ignore any research funded by companies or special interest groups? Certainly not. These groups provide invaluable funding for scientific research. Furthermore, science has many safeguards in place to catch instances of bias that affect research outcomes. Ultimately, misleading results will be corrected as science proceeds; however, this process takes time. Meanwhile, it pays to examine studies funded by industry or special interest groups with extra care. Are the results consistent with other independently funded studies? What do other scientists have to say about this research? A little examination can go a long way towards identifying bias associated with the funding source.

questions.stem: What does the passage mainly discuss regarding scientific research?
questions.explanation:
【答案】D （主旨题）
【判型】What does the passage mainly discuss regarding scientific research? 中的 mainly
discuss 直接锁定主旨题。
【拆句】题干主句是 What does the passage mainly discuss，regarding scientific research 是介
词短语作状语，限定讨论的对象范围，句式平铺直叙、无陷阱。
【选项】A) 无中生有：选项核心词在全文找不到主线对应
Its foundation 中的 foundation（基础／根基）在 P1~P4 中找不到对应；原文一次都
未把科研的‘基础’作为讨论对象。
B) 以偏概全：拿某段／某句的局部当全文主旨
we reap the rewards from this science 中确实出现 rewards，但只是一句话铺垫，
P2~P4 都未围绕 ‘rewards’ 展开；Its rewards 把局部一句话上升为全文主旨。
C) 无中生有＋时态错位
Its prospect 中的 prospect（前景／未来展望）在 P1~P4 中无对应——作者讨论的是
‘现状’与‘应对方式’，未对科研的未来作出预测。
D) ✓ 正确
most scientific research is funded by government grants, companies doing research and
development, and non-profit foundations
↔ Its funding
Funding for science has changed with the times ↔ Its funding
Its funding 中的 Its 回指 scientific research，funding 则覆盖了 P1~P4 反复讨论的资
助来源、资助偏差、资助审慎度——是唯一覆盖四段共同主线的选项。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about researchers like birdwatchers and rock collectors?

options.label: A
options.text: They have little access to government funding.

options.label: B
options.text: They can do research with limited resources.

options.label: C
options.text: They can do amateur work in their own fields.

options.label: D
options.text: They have no means for large-scale research.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题）
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about researchers like birdwatchers and rock
collectors? 询问对某一特定群体的事实陈述，是典型细节题。
【拆句】主干是 What do we learn from the passage about researchers，like birdwatchers and
rock collectors 是举例修饰 researchers，结构清晰、无陷阱。
【定位】Most of us can't afford to do nuclear research as a private hobby, but birdwatchers, rock
collectors, and others can do real research on a limited budget.
我们大多数人无法把核研究当成私人爱好，但观鸟人、岩石收藏者等人可以用有限的预算做
真正的研究。
【选项】A) 无中生有：原文未提即排除
They have little access to government funding 在 P2 中找不到对应陈述——原文只
说他们自掏腰包，并未对‘是否能拿到政府资助’作判断。
B) ✓ 正确
on a limited budget ↔ with limited resources
can do real research ↔ can do research
B 项 They can do research with limited resources 把定位句 can do real research
on a limited budget 中的能力与资源条件一一对应替换，与预判完全吻合。
C) 偷换概念：把原文措辞替换为相近但意义偏移的表达
原文 can do real research 强调的是‘真正的研究’，而 amateur work in their own
fields 把‘真正研究’偷换成‘业余工作’，且 in their own fields 也是原文未提的限定。
D) 张冠李戴＋绝对化
They have no means for large-scale research 把 Most of us can't afford to do
nuclear research as a private hobby 中‘多数人’的处境强行套到 ‘birdwatchers, rock
collectors’ 头上，并把陈述绝对化为 no means。

questions.stem: What would scientific studies look like in a perfect world according to the author?
questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题）
【判型】What would scientific studies look like in a perfect world according to the author?
用 would look like 询问作者对一个特定情境下的事实描述。
【拆句】主句是 What would scientific studies look like，in a perfect world 与 according to
the author 都是状语修饰，按情境＋来源给约束，句式无陷阱。
【定位】In a perfect world, money wouldn't matter—all scientific studies would be
completely objective.
在一个完美的世界里，钱不会成为问题——所有的科学研究都会是完全客观的。
【选项】A) ✓ 正确
completely objective ↔ totally unbiased
A 项 They would be totally unbiased 用 unbiased 反向定义 objective，用 totally 替
换 completely，与预判 ‘完全客观’ 一一对应。
B) 偷换概念：把比较项当成主张
原文 Drug research sponsored by the pharmaceutical(制药的) industry is more
likely to end up favoring the drug under consideration than studies sponsored
by government grants or charitable organizations 仅把独立资助的研究当作偏差较
小的对照，并未说‘完美世界里所有研究都应独立资助’。
C) 无中生有：选项关键词在原文无对应
They would be responsibly conducted 中的 responsibly 在 P3 中没有对应词或近义
概念，属凭语感想当然。
D) 无中生有＋话题外推
They would be strictly supervised 引入‘严格监管’这一原文未涉及的维度。原文只谈
‘客观’，未谈‘监管’。

questions.stem: What does the author say about companies and special interest groups?

options.label: A
options.text: They try hard to pull down the safeguards for research.

options.label: B
options.text: They make extra efforts to research their own products.

options.label: C
options.text: They provide valuable resources for scientific research.

options.label: D
options.text: They reap the most benefits from scientific research.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】What does the author say about companies and special interest groups? 询问作者对
某一明确主体的具体陈述，是细节题。
【拆句】主句是 What does the author say about companies and special interest groups?，
about 引导的介词短语锁定主体对象，句式简短无陷阱。
【定位】These groups provide invaluable funding for scientific research.
这些团体为科学研究提供了极其宝贵的资金。
【选项】A) 与原文相反：把肯定语句逆转
原文 science has many safeguards in place to catch instances of bias that affect
research outcomes 明确指出科学有 safeguards，作者也未指控这些团体‘试图打
掉’safeguards；A 项 They try hard to pull down the safeguards for research 直接
与原文事实对立。
B) 过度推断：把现象升级为意图
原文只说企业资助的研究‘更可能偏向其产品’（more likely to end up favoring the
drug under consideration），并未说企业‘额外努力地’去研究自家产品；B 项 They
make extra efforts to research their own products 是从结果反推动机，越界。
C) ✓ 正确
provide invaluable funding for scientific research ↔
provide valuable resources for scientific research
C 项 They provide valuable resources for scientific research 与定位句结构、谓语、
宾语短语高度对齐，是定位句最纯粹的同义改写。
D) 无中生有＋绝对化
They reap the most benefits from scientific research 中‘获益最多’这一比较级在 P4
中找不到任何对应陈述——原文谈他们是‘出资方’，未谈‘获益方排序’。

questions.stem: What does the author think of research funded by industry or special interest groups?

options.label: A
options.text: Its recommendations should be examined for feasibility.

options.label: B
options.text: Its misleading results should be corrected in time.

options.label: C
options.text: Its validity should be checked with additional care.

options.label: D
options.text: Its hidden biases should be identified independently.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】What does the author think of research funded by industry or special interest
groups? 询问作者对特定 research 的明确看法，属于带观点色彩的细节题，仍可单点定位
作者评价句。
【拆句】主句是 What does the author think of research，funded by industry or special
interest groups 是 research 的过去分词后置定语，相当于 the research that is funded
by…，句式直白无陷阱。
【定位】Meanwhile, it pays to examine studies funded by industry or special interest groups with
extra care.
同时，对工业界或特殊利益团体资助的研究多加小心地审视，是值得的。
【选项】A) 无中生有＋话题偏移
原文谈的是‘核查这类研究的结论是否可靠’，并非‘检查其建议的可行性’；Its
recommendations should be examined for feasibility 中 recommendations 与
feasibility 都是无中生有的概念。
B) 张冠李戴：把全局机制改成对单一对象的建议
原文 misleading results will be corrected as science proceeds 是说科学过程会自我
纠错，而 B 项 Its misleading results should be corrected in time 把这一过程改写为
作者对企业资助研究的具体建议，并加入 in time 这一原文未提的时限。
C) ✓ 正确
examine…with extra care ↔ Its validity should be checked with additional care

C 项 Its validity should be checked with additional care 把作者 ‘要带着额外的小心

D) 偷换概念＋强加限定
原文 A little examination can go a long way towards identifying bias associated
with the funding source 只说‘审视可帮助识别偏差’，并未要求‘独立地
（independently）识别 hidden biases’；D 项强加 hidden 与 independently 两层原
文没说的限制。

title: 2024年06月真题·第1套 · 选词填空

paragraphs.text: It's well known that physical exercise is beneficial not just to physical health but also to mental health. Yet whereas most countries have  [26]  , evidence-backed guidelines on the type and intensity of exercise  [27]  for various physical health benefits, such guidelines do not yet exist for exercise and mood. This is  [28]  due to a lack of necessary evidence. However, a new systematic review brings us usefully up to-date on the current findings in this area.

Before  [29]  into some of the key take-aways, an important  [30]  made in the review is between aerobic exercise and anaerobic. The former  [31]  such things as walking, jogging and cycling and means exercising in such a way that your body is able to use oxygen to burn fat for energy. In contrast, anaerobic exercise—such as lifting heavy weights—is of such  [32]  intensity that your body does not have time to use oxygen to create energy and so instead it breaks down glucose(葡萄糖) in your blood or muscles.

Beginning first with the influence of exercise intensity on the mood benefits of aerobic exercise, the researchers, led by John Chan at Shenzhen University, found  [33]  results from 19 relevant studies. Some favoured higher intensity, others low, while seven studies found that intensity made no  [34]  to mood benefits.

In relation to the intensity of anaerobic exercise, however, the results were far clearer—the optimum(最佳选择) for improving mood is  [35]  intensity, perhaps because low intensity is too dull while high intensity is too unpleasant.

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】D) detailed
形容词
【词性槽】have ___, evidence-backed guidelines，修饰 guidelines
【依据】与 evidence-backed 并列修饰"指南"，最贴的是"详细的"
guidelines 的常见修饰是"详细的、有循证支撑的"——detailed, evidence-backed
guidelines 正是常见地道搭配；且与下文 such guidelines do not yet exist for exercise
and mood 形成"运动健身的指南详尽，但情绪方向还没有"的对比。
【竞争词】B) contradictory "相互矛盾的指南"逻辑不通
contradictory 表"自相矛盾的"，作者要赞大多数国家有靠谱的指南，不会说"自相矛盾"。
J) moderate moderate 修饰"强度"而非"指南"
moderate 在本文专指"中等强度"（见 35 题），用来修饰 guidelines 既不搭配也无意义。
O) vigorous vigorous 修饰"运动"，不修饰"指南"
vigorous 常与 exercise/activity 搭配表"剧烈的"，无法形容指南文本。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】M) required
动词
【词性槽】the type and intensity of exercise ___ for various…，后置定语动词
【依据】be required for = 为……所必需
原句要表达"为获得各种身体健康益处所需要的运动种类与强度"——guidelines on the
type and intensity of exercise required for…physical health benefits，required for 与
"for various physical health benefits" 自然搭配。
【竞争词】K) notified notify 的对象是人，不是"运动"
notify 表"通知（某人）"，主语通常是"通知的内容"，而"运动被通知"语义荒谬；且 notified for
也非地道搭配，应是 notified of/about。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】L) partly
副词
【词性槽】be 动词 + ___ + due to，空处修饰整个表语
【依据】下文转折"However"暗示"部分原因"而非全部
空后是 due to a lack of necessary evidence. However, a new systematic review brings
us usefully up to-date on the current findings in this area.，"However" 表明证据并非
全无、综述已带来更新，所以缺乏证据只是"部分"原因，partly 与下文逻辑天然吻合。
【竞争词】N) traditionally "传统上"与上文"目前还没有指南"矛盾
上文 such guidelines do not yet exist for exercise and mood 讲的是"目前"的状况，
traditionally 意为"传统上、历来"，时间指向错位；况且"传统上由于缺证据"读起来也不符合科
学综述的客观语气。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 N) —— traditionally 与"due to"看似自然，但与下文 However 矛
盾。traditionally 单看本句"传统上是由于缺乏证据"也成立，副词位、句法都对；防坑：副
词空务必读到下一句的逻辑词——However, a new systematic review brings us usefully
up to-date 已部分推翻"缺证据"的说法，所以只能是"部分原因"partly。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】F) dipping
动词
【词性槽】介词 Before 后 + ___ into，需动名词
【依据】dip into = 涉足、稍稍探讨某话题
下文 Before __(29)__ into some of the key take-aways, an important __(30)__ made in
the review is between aerobic exercise and anaerobic. 是过渡句——"在涉足/简略谈及
这些要点之前，先要……"。dip into 正是"稍微进入、涉足"的固定搭配，与"key take-
aways（关键要点）"搭配自然，且贴合综述类文章的口吻。
【竞争词】H) falling fall into 意为"陷入/掉入"，多含被动或贬义
fall into 常表"陷入（困境/陷阱/分类）"，逻辑上不是作者主动"探讨"key take-aways，而是"掉
进去"，与作者掌控话题节奏的语气不符。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】G) distinction
名词
【词性槽】an important ___ made…between A and B
【依据】make a distinction between A and B = 区分 A 与 B
空后明确是 between aerobic exercise and anaerobic——在有氧与无氧之间作"区分"。
make a distinction between 是地道搭配，且下文整段都在分别解释两类运动的差别，正
是"区分"在展开。
【竞争词】C) decision make a decision 不与 between A and B 这样接"两类区分"
make a decision 一般搭 about/on，且表"在 A 与 B 之间作决定"时是二选一，本文并不是
要"在有氧和无氧之间二选一"，而是要把它们"区分开"以便分别讨论。语义指向不符。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】I) involves
动词
【词性槽】The former ___ such things as…，主语后缺谓语
【依据】involves such things as = 包括诸如……这样的事物
involve + such things as 是地道搭配，表"包括、涉及（举例）"。文中要表达"前者（有氧
运动）包括走路、慢跑、骑车这样的项目"，involve 既符合搭配又符合"举例罗列"的语义。

title: 2024年06月真题·第1套 · 长篇匹配（Why Do Americans Work So）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: How will we all keep busy when we only have to work 15 hours a week? That was the question that worried the British economist John Maynard Keynes when he wrote his short essay "Economic Possibilities for Our Grandchildren" in 1930. Over the next century, he predicted, the economy would become so productive that people would barely need to work at all. For a while, it looked like Keynes was right. In 1930 the average working week was 47 hours in the United States. But by 1970, the number of hours Americans worked on average had fallen to slightly less than 39.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: But then something changed. Instead of continuing to decline, the duration of the working week remained stable. It has stayed at just below 40 hours for nearly five decades. So what happened? Why are people working just as much today as in 1970?

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: There would be no mystery in this if Keynes had been wrong about the power of technology to increase the economy's productivity, which he thought would lead to a standard of living "between four and eight times as high as it is today." But Keynes got that right: Technology has made the economy massively more productive. According to Benjamin M.Friedman, an economist at Harvard, the U.S. economy is right on track to reach Keynes's eight-fold(八倍) multiple by 2029. That is a century after the last data Keynes would have had access to.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: In a new paper, Friedman tries to figure out why that increased productivity has not translated into increased leisure time. Perhaps people just never feel materially satisfied, always wanting more money to buy the next new thing. This is a theory that appeals to many economists. "This argument is, at best, far from sufficient," he writes. If that were the case, why did the duration of the working week decline in the first place?

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Another theory Friedman considers is that, in an era of ever fewer settings that provide effective opportunities for personal connections and relationships, people may place more value on the socializing that happens at work. There is support for this theory. Many people today consider colleagues as friends. But Friedman argues that the evidence for this theory is far from conclusive. Many workers report that they would like to spend more time with family, rather than at work. Furthermore, this theory cannot explain the change in trend in the U.S. working week in the 1970s.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: A third possibility proves more convincing for Friedman. That is: American inequality means that the gains of increasing productivity are not widely shared by everyone. In other words, most Americans are too poor to work less. Unlike the other two explanations Friedman considers, this one fits chronologically(按年代). Inequality declined in America during the period following World War II, along with the duration of the working week. But since the early 1970s it has risen dramatically.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Keynes's prediction of a shorter working week rests on the idea that the standard of living would continue rising for everyone. But Friedman says that this is not what has happened. Although Keynes's eight-fold figure holds up for the economy as a whole, it is not at all the case for the median(中位数的) American worker. For them, output by 2029 is likely to be around 3.5 times what it was when Keynes was writing. This is a bit below his four-to eight-fold predicted range.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: This can be seen in the median worker's income over this time period, complete with a shift in 1973 that fits in precisely with when the working week stopped shrinking. According to Friedman, between 1947 and 1973 the average hourly wage for normal workers (those who were not in management roles) in private industries other than agriculture nearly doubled in terms of what their money could buy. But by 2013 the average hourly wage for ordinary workers had fallen 5 percent from the 1973 level in terms of actual purchasing power. Thus, though American incomes may have gone up since 1973, the amount that American workers can actually buy with their money has gone down. For most Americans, then, the magic of increasing productivity stopped working around 1973. Thus, they had to keep working just as much in order to maintain their standard of living.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: What Keynes predicted was a very optimistic version of what economists call technological unemployment. This is the idea that less labor will be necessary because machines can do so much. In Keynes's vision, the resulting unemployment would be distributed more or less evenly across society in the form of increased leisure. But Friedman says that, for Americans, reality is much darker. Americans now have a labor market in which millions of people—those with fewer skills and less education—are seeking whatever poorly paid work they can get. This is confirmed by a recent poll that found that, for half of hourly workers, their top concern is not that they work too much but that they work too little. This is most likely not because they like their jobs so much. Rather, we can assume it is because they need the money.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: This explanation leaves an important question. If the very rich—the workers who have reaped above-average gains from the increased productivity since Keynes's time—can afford to work less, why do they continue to work so much? (Indeed, research has shown that the highest earners in America tend to work the most.) Friedman believes that for many top earners, work is a labor of love. They are doing work they care about and are interested in, and doing more of it is not necessarily a burden. For them, it may even be a pleasure. These top earners derive meaning from their jobs and work is an important part of how they think of themselves. And, of course, they are compensated for it at a level that makes it worth their while.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Friedman concludes that the prosperity(繁荣) Keynes predicted is here. After all, the economy as a whole has grown even more brilliantly than he expected. But for most Americans, that prosperity is nowhere to be seen. And, as a result, neither are those shorter working weeks.

title: 2024年06月真题·第1套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: Lao Zi once said, "Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner."

People-pleasing, or seeking self-worth through others' approval, is unproductive and an exhausting way to go through life. Why do we allow what others think of us to have so much power over how we feel about ourselves? If it's true that you can't please all people all of the time, wouldn't it make sense to stop trying?

Unfortunately, sense often isn't driving our behavior. For social beings who desire love and belonging, wanting to be liked, and caring about the effect we have on others, is healthy and allows us to make connections. However, where we get into trouble is when our self-worth is dependent upon whether we win someone's approval or not.

This need to be liked can be traced back to when we were children and were completely dependent on others to take care of us: Small children are not just learning how to walk and communicate, they are also trying to learn how the world works. We learn about who we are and what is expected of us based on interactions with others, so, to a four-year-old, if Mommy or Daddy doesn't like him or her, there is the danger that they will abandon them. We need to understand that when we desperately want someone to approve of us, it's being driven by that little kid part of us that is still terrified of abandonment.

As you become more capable of providing yourself with the approval you seek, your need for external validation will start to vanish, leaving you stronger, more confident, and yes, happier in your life. Imagine how much time we lose each moment we restrain our authentic selves in an effort to be liked.

If we base our worth on the opinions of others, we cheat ourselves of the power to shape our experiences and embrace life not only for others but also for ourselves, because ultimately, there is no difference. So embrace the cliché(老话) and love yourself as it's highly doubtful that you'll regret it.

title: 2024年06月真题·第1套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom. However, a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible. In reality, education does an aging brain good.

Throughout life, people's brains constantly renovate themselves. In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new.

Of course, that doesn't mean the brain isn't affected by the effects of time. Just as height usually declines over the years, so does brain volume: Humans lose about 4 percent every decade starting in their 40s. But that reduction doesn't necessarily make people think slower; as long as we are alive and functioning, we can alter our brains with new information and experiences.

In fact, scientists now suspect accumulating novel experiences, facts, and skills can keep people's minds more flexible. New pathways can strengthen our ever-changing mental structure, even as the brain shrinks.

Conventional fixes like word puzzles and brain-training apps can contribute to mental durability. Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy.

A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. Research about aging adults who take on new enterprises shows improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease. Openness—a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge—may also help folks pass brain tests. Some folks are born with this take-in-the-world attitude, but those who aren't as genetically gifted aren't necessarily out of luck. While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. That's why brain scientist Richard Kennedy says "It's not that old dogs can't learn new tricks. It's that maybe old dogs don't realize why they should."

title: 2023年12月真题·第3套 · 选词填空

paragraphs.text: When people set out to improve their health, they usually take a familiar path: starting a healthy diet, getting better sleep, and doing regular exercise. Each of these behaviors is important, of course, but they all  [26]  on physical health—and a growing body of research suggests that social health is just as, if not more, important to  [27]  well-being.

One recent study published in the journal PLOS ONE, for example, found that the strength of a person's social circle was a better  [28]  of self-reported stress, happiness and well-being levels than fitness tracker data on physical activity, heart rate and sleep. That finding suggests that the "  [29]  self" represented by endless amounts of health data doesn't tell the whole  [30]  .
There's also a qualified self, which is who I am, what are my activities, my social network, and all of these aspects are not  [31]  in any of these measurements.

This idea is supported by plenty of  [32]  research. Studies have shown that social support—whether it comes from friends, family members or a spouse—is  [33]  associated with better mental and physical health. A rich social life, these studies suggest, can lower stress levels, improve mood, encourage positive health behaviors and discourage damaging ones, boost heart health and improve illness  [34]  rates.

Social isolation, meanwhile, is linked to higher rates of physical diseases and mental health conditions. It's a significant problem,  [35]  since loneliness is emerging as a widespread public health problem in many countries.

title: 2023年12月真题·第3套 · 长篇匹配（Teenagers and social net）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: As a parent of two boys at primary school, I worry about the issues associated with teenagers and social media. Newspapers are constantly filled with frightening accounts of drug addiction and aggressive behaviour supposedly caused by violent video games. But even when these accounts touch on real concerns, they do not really reflect the great mass of everyday teenage social behaviour: the online chat, the texting, the surfing, and the emergence of a new teenage sphere that is conducted digitally.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: New technologies always provoke generational panic, which usually has more to do with adult fears than with the lives of teenagers. In the 1930s, parents worried that radio was gaining "an irresistible hold of their children". In the 80s, the great danger was the Sony Walkman(随身听). When you look at today's digital activity, the facts are much more positive than you might expect.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Indeed, social scientists who study young people have found that their digital use can be inventive and even beneficial. This is true not just in terms of their social lives, but their education too. So if you use a ton of social media, do you become unable, or unwilling, to engage in face-to-face contact? The evidence suggests not. Research by Amanda Lenhart of the Pew Research Centre, a US think tank, found that the most passionate texters are also the kids most likely to spend time with friends in person. One form of socialising doesn't replace the other. It expands it.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: "Kids still spend time face to face," Lenhart says. Indeed, as they get older and are given more freedom, they often ease up on social networking. Early on, the web is their "third space", but by the late teens, it's replaced in reaction to greater independence. They have to be on Facebook, to know what's going on among friends and family, but they are ambivalent(有矛盾心理的) about it, says Rebecca Eynon, a research fellow at the Oxford Internet Institute, who has interviewed about 200 British teenagers over three years. As they gain experience with living online, they begin to adjust their behaviour, struggling with new communication skills, as they do in the real world.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Parents are wrong to worry that kids don't care about privacy. In fact, they spend hours changing Facebook settings or using quick-delete sharing tools, such as Snapchat, to minimise their traces. Or they post a photograph on Instagram, have a pleasant conversation with friends and then delete it so that no traces remain.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: This is not to say that kids always use good judgment. Like everyone else, they make mistakes—sometimes serious ones. But working out how to behave online is a new social skill. While there's plenty of drama and messiness online, it is not, for most teens, a cycle of non-stop abuse: a Pew study found only 15% of teens said someone had bullied them online in the last 12 months.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: But surely all this short-form writing is affecting literacy? Certainly, teachers worry. They say that kids use overly casual language and text-speak in writing, and don't have as much patience for long reading and complex arguments. Yet studies of first-year college papers suggest these anxieties may be partly based on misguided nostalgia(怀旧). When Stanford University scholar Andrea Lunsford gathered data on the rates of errors in "freshman composition" papers going back to 1917, she found that they were virtually identical to today.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: But even as error rates stayed stable, student essays have blossomed in size and complexity. They are now six times longer and, unlike older "what I did this summer" essays, they offer arguments supported by evidence. Why? Computers have vastly increased the ability of students to gather information, sample different points of view and write more fluidly.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: When linguist Naomi Baron studied students, instant messaging even there she found surprisingly rare usage of short forms such as "u" for "you", and as students got older, they began to write in more grammatical sentences. That is because they want to appear more adult, and they know how adults are expected to write. Clearly, teaching teens formal writing is still crucial, but texting probably isn't destroying their ability to learn it.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: It is probably true that fewer kids are heavy readers compared with two generations ago, when cheap paperbacks boosted rates of reading. But even back then, a minority of people—perhaps 20%—were lifelong heavy readers, and it was cable TV not the internet, that struck a blow at that culture in the 1980s. Still, 15% or more of kids are found to be deeply bookish. In fact, the online world offers kids remarkable opportunities to become literate and creative because young people can now publish ideas not just to their friends, but to the world. And it turns out that when they write for strangers, their sense of "authentic audience" makes them work harder, push themselves further, and create powerful new communicative forms.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Few would deny that too much time online can be harmful. Some of the dangers are emotional: hurting someone from a distance is not the same as hurting them face to face. If we're lucky, the legal environment will change to make teenagers' online lives less likely to haunt them later on. Just last week, California passed a law allowing minors to demand that internet firms erase their digital past and the EU has considered similar legislation.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Distraction is also a serious issue. When kids switch from chat to music to homework, they are indeed likely to have trouble doing each task well. And studies show that pupils don't fact-check information online—"smart searching" is a skill schools need to teach urgently. It's also true that too much social networking and game playing can cut into schoolwork and sleep. This is precisely why parents still need to set firm boundaries around it, as with any other distraction.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: So what's the best way to cope? The same boring old advice that applies to everything in parenting: moderation. Rebecca Eynon argues that it's key to model good behaviour. Parents who stare non-stop at their phones and don't read books are likely to breed kids who will do the same. As ever, we ought to be careful about our own behaviour.

title: 2023年12月真题·第3套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: In the history of horse racing, few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum. Today, three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time.
Red Rum was passed around to several owners before being purchased for Noel Le Mar. The agent who made the purchase was the now-legendary horse trainer Donald "Ginger" McCain.

It wasn't apparent at the time, but Red Rum had a serious bone disease in his foot. For many horses (and many trainers) this would mean the end of a racing career before it even began. For Ginger and Red Rum, though, it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome.

Red Rum's true talent came out in steeplechases(障碍赛马). His power, speed and jumping ability carried him to his first Grand National title in 1973. The very next year, Red Rum returned to take his second title. He was the first horse to take successive firsts since Reynoldstown in 1935-1936. Red Rum's spirit and grace had already begun to charm the leagues of Grand National fans.

In the following two years, Red Rum lost out on the title, coming in second both times. When he returned in 1977 to try again, he was largely regarded as past his prime. He was 12 years old and not expected to place highly. He surprised sporting fans around the world when he came in a remarkable 25 lengths ahead of the nearest horse, taking his third Grand National win. To this day, Red Rum's third win is known as one of the greatest moments in horse racing history.

Red Rum was headed for the Grand National once again in 1978 but suffered an injury in one of his heels shortly before the race. He was retired soon after, but his public life and fame by no means decreased with the end of his career. Red Rum traveled all over the country for various engagements. He often led pre-race parades at Aintree Racecourse and was a popular guest at charity benefits and public events.

title: 2023年12月真题·第3套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts. It is quite horrifying to see people being guided by some unknown force. But how wise is it, really, to let your instincts drive your decisions?

In the decision-making process, relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you. Simply "feeling" that something is right or should be done is highly subjective and can drown you.

On the other hand, there is a more rational approach to making decisions. Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions. These reduce the likelihood of errors and increase the chances of success. Big, systematic data is mostly the foundation of most of our decisions, personal and business alike. But with its extreme usability comes a complication: what do you do if you strongly feel something should not be done, even if the data insists that it should?

This seemingly easy question is what drives the need to understand the relationship between instincts and data in the decision-making process. Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions.

Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences or information, which acknowledges that instinctive decisions have worked in the past. Decisions are not about making the choice and braving the consequences because you want to blindly trust your instincts. They are about combining your inner wisdom with the knowledge of systematic data to make the best decisions.

Sometimes, rational analysis and data are impractical to be employed in certain situations. Absence of definitive criteria, and time and resource constraints, and novel situations are instances which limit the practicality of data. The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you. In these situations, instincts can help you make effective and quick decisions.

Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions. It reduces the chances of making mistakes, and has increasingly become a favorite approach to decision-making among leaders of today.

questions.stem: What does the author say businesspeople often do?

【答案】D （细节题）
【判型】What does the author say businesspeople often do? 问的是「商人通常做什么」这一可
在原文逐字核实的客观行为，不含 infer/imply。
【拆句】题干主干是 What does the author say businesspeople often do?，what 作宾语前置；
the author say 是插入成分，可剥离；剥离后等价于「Businesspeople often do what?」
结构平铺，无陷阱。
【定位】People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts.
商界人士常常基于自己的个人感觉或直觉做决策。
【选项】A) 无中生有
原文用 unknown force 比喻直觉的神秘性，并未让商人「弄清未知力量」；Strive to
make sense of some unknown forces 凭空给出动作。
B) 与原文相反
原文说商人「常凭感觉决策」，Avoid being driven by their own feeling 却说「避免
被感觉驱动」，完全反向。
C) 张冠李戴
relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to
support you 是作者给「合理使用直觉」开的条件，并非商人「实际正在做的事」。
D) ✓ 正确
make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts ↔
Rely on instincts in decision-making
预判「依赖直觉作决策」与 Rely on instincts in decision-making 高度重合，正确项
锁定。

in order to make informed decisions 是表目的的不定式状语；句式简单。
【定位】Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions.

【选项】A) 答非所问
原文 These reduce the likelihood of errors 说数据与分析「降低出错概率」，The
likelihood of errors 只是数据带来的「结果」，不是「应当考虑的因素」。

Data and analysis ↔ Systematic data and analysis

C) 无中生有

D) 偷换概念
原文把 personal feelings or instincts 视作「常被依赖却需谨慎」的对象，并未把它与
business strategies 并列为「做明智决策的因素」。

【定位】Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in

Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 是「直觉的支撑机
制」，不是题干问的「矛盾时的解决办法」。
B) 无中生有
原文从未让人「比较谁更可靠」，Figure out which of the two is more reliable 是凭
空增加的取舍动作。
C) ✓ 正确
using data and instincts in conjunction ↔ Combine the two together

锁定。
D) 与原文相反

Prioritize instincts over data 却把直觉摆在数据之上，反向。

础薄弱的同学要看清「factors」才是从句修饰对象，而不是「we」。
【定位】The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you.
唯一可行的办法，是依靠你的直觉告诉你的东西。
【选项】A) 与原文相反

questions.stem: What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author?

options.label: A

options.label: B

【答案】A （细节题）
【判型】What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 问的是
「让决策成为最佳」的所需条件，是原文有明确句子可对应的细节，并非要从全文归纳的
主旨。
【拆句】题干 What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 句
型为「it takes sth for sb/sth to do sth」，what 替换 sth 提前；for decisions 是 take
的逻辑主语；to become the best 是真正的目的不定式。看懂这个句型是关键，否则容易
把题干误读成主旨题。
【定位】Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions.
把直觉与理性分析结合起来，能产出周全的决策。
【选项】A) ✓ 正确
Combining instinctive and rational analysis ↔ Applying instincts and data in conjunction
using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions ↔
Applying instincts and data in conjunction
预判「直觉＋理性分析联用」与 Applying instincts and data in conjunction 完全对
应，且 P4 与 P7 双句佐证，正确项锁定。
B) 无中生有

来源的扩张表述。
C) 以偏概全
Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 只是说直觉以经验
为后盾，并不等于「让决策变最佳」的充分条件，Recalling what has actually worked
in the past 把直觉一侧的支撑当成全部条件。
D) 以偏概全
you want to blindly trust your instincts 提到「不要盲目相信直觉」，但这只是「最佳
决策」的一个否定性前提，不是充分条件，Refraining from trusting instincts
arbitrarily 把单一前提当成全部条件。

title: 2023年12月真题·第2套 · 选词填空

paragraphs.text: A number of studies have looked at how family life can affect productivity and satisfaction in the workplace. However, there has been  [26]  little research on the influence of leisure activities. So Ciara Kelly and colleagues recruited 129 hobbyists to look at how the time spent on their hobbies  [27]  their work life.

The researchers found that when participants spent longer than  [28]  on their leisure activity, their belief in their ability to perform their job was strengthened. But this was only the  [29]  when they had a serious hobby that was dissimilar to their job, or when their hobby was similar to their work but they only did it  [30]  . When their hobby was both serious and similar to their job, then spending more time on it actually decreased their work  [31]  .

Why might that be? To maintain a serious hobby, people need to invest significant psychological resources, say the authors—so if the activity has the same kinds of demands as their work, they may be left  [32]  and unable to perform well at their job. But if their hobby is quite different from their career, it may not  [33]  in the same way but instead help them develop other knowledge and skills that can  [34]  their confidence at work. "Consider a scientist who is a keen rock climber," says Kelly. "Since climbing is so far  [35]  from their day-to-day work activities, they can still recover from the demands of their job with plenty of resources."

title: 2023年12月真题·第2套 · 长篇匹配（More fathers are taking ）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Attitudes towards paternity leave(陪产假) have drastically changed in America in the last five years as more fathers feel comfortable taking extended time off, but gender bias persists when it comes to career prospects and the home, according to a new study of working parents.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Research by the Boston College Center for Work & Family, which surveyed new parents at four large US companies who were qualified for taking at least six weeks paid parental leave, found that 81% of the 1,240 employees surveyed said the notion of fathers taking leave has become more acceptable.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Of those surveyed, 62% of fathers took the maximum amount of time off compared to 93% of mothers, and around three-quarters of workers said their employer was equally supportive of mothers and fathers taking parental leave and over half said leave policies had made workplace culture better.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The US is one of only three countries in the world not to offer statutory(法定的) paid leave, but increasingly states and companies are starting to take up the issue. So far, eight states and the District of Columbia have their own paid family leave laws.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Brad Harrington, executive director of the center and lead author of the study, estimates only 20% to 30% of companies in the US offer paid parental leave. He feels the research findings reflect an obvious change in corporate attitudes to new fathers taking time off.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: "We did a study on paternity leave five years ago. Compared with those findings, these numbers were shocking to me. I did not expect 80% of people to say the organisation finds dads taking this leave acceptable and three-quarters to say it's equally supportive of women and men taking leave," Harrington said.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The previous study found that nearly three-quarters of fathers saw two to four weeks as an appropriate duration for paternity leave and 76% said they would prefer not to take all their time off at once.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Since then, there have been a number of legal cases against companies involving paternity leave—including cases against JPMorgan Chase and Estee Lauder—which have helped put pressure on companies to make their parental leave policies gender neutral.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: However, the study also shows how traditional gender roles endure both at work, where more women than men reported changes in their perceived career potential, and at home—even among workers who claim to have a strong desire for equality.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: The vast majority of men, 97%, said one of the top reasons to take leave was to share caregiving with their partner. But when they were asked about how caregiving and household tasks were divided, their answers painted a different picture. While about 75% of employees said both genders should give the same amount of care, the majority of men and nearly half of women admitted that in reality the female actually did most of it. A tiny fraction, 2%, of men said they did more of the childcare.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Men and women's experiences of the return to work following parental leave were also considerably different. Of the women surveyed, 32% reported a downturn in their job satisfaction, while 14% said it increased. In comparison, 17% of men said their job satisfaction went down and 20% said it went up. Meanwhile, more women reported an increase in their responsibilities and manager expectations after childbirth. Half of the women said they used flexible work arrangements after becoming a parent, while just 27% of men did. Similar percentages of men and women said they enjoyed their careers and that it gave them a sense of achievement, while around half of women and 44% of men said it was a key part of their identity.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: On the subject of career advancement, 59% of women and 49% of men said leave could be limiting and both genders said they feared it would have an impact on their progress long-term. But on opportunity for promotion, more than double the number of women, 30% compared with 15% of men, believed their chances to be lower after becoming a parent. Despite progress, the struggle for women to reach the highest positions of power is demonstrated in this year's Fortune 500 list, which featured a record 33 female CEOs, but this still represents a tiny fraction of the total.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Harrington said culture change depends on companies putting more focus on men and their responsibilities. "By that I mean companies need to give men paternity leave and encourage men to take time off to be with their kids early on in the kids' life. They also need to recognise that men have to make significant adjustments when they become parents. Companies cannot do all these things to enhance women's advancement and then turn around and say, 'Oh, but we don't expect the men to take over for the women at home.'"

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: In May, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Outten & Golden LLP announced a historic class-action $5m settlement with JPMorgan Chase on behalf of male employees who claim they were illegally denied access to paid parental leave. Derek Rotondo, 35, filed the discrimination charge against his company after he was allegedly told by his HR department that mothers were considered primary caregivers. Thus, they were allowed to take 16 weeks of paid parental leave. Fathers, however, could take just two weeks.

paragraphs.label: O
paragraphs.text: The father of two from Columbus, Ohio, who still works at the company as an associate and investigator, said he has witnessed a "domino effect(多米诺效应)" across companies since the settlement, but that there is still substantial progress to be made towards changing attitudes towards paternity leave.

paragraphs.label: P
paragraphs.text: "I do think there's still some way to go…there's still going to be sort of the unstated expectation for new dads to essentially come right back to work, but I think the research is showing that's starting to change." He said equal parental leave is an essential component to creating gender equality in the workplace. "The old standard of women staying home, having babies and cooking doesn't apply and hasn't applied for a long time."

paragraphs.text: Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success.

Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important. While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.

One reason having a rival can enhance your venture's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.

The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making.

paragraphs.text: A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which—apart from the obvious differences—is similar to what a computer does. The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?

For most scientists, the answer is no. So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes. Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.

However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.

The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.

The benefits of multitasking are clear. Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.

questions.stem: What does a "multitasker" originally refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once.

options.label: B
options.text: A skilled worker executing more than one task at the same time.

options.label: C
options.text: A sophisticated technology doing several tasks effectively at once.

options.label: D
options.text: An efficient person able to perform multiple tasks at the same time.

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （词义句意题）
【判型】题干 What does a "multitasker" originally refer to 直接问一个词「原本指什么」，考的
是文中对该词来源含义的界定。
【拆句】句子主干是 What does a "multitasker" originally refer to，结构平铺，refer to 意为「指
代、指的是」，originally 作状语修饰 refer to，意为「最初指的是」。无陷阱。
【定位】The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an
operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time.
这个概念确实来自科技领域，在那里它被用来指一种能够同时执行多项任务的操作系统。
【选项】A) ✓ 正确
an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time ↔
An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once
预判要的「能同时多任务的操作系统」与 An operating system capable of doing
several tasks at once 完全吻合，主体、能力、同时性三点都对上。
B) 偷换概念
A skilled worker（熟练工人）把主体说成人，而原词最初指的是操作系统，主体张冠
李戴。
C) 偷换概念
A sophisticated technology（一种复杂技术）只取了原文「来自科技领域」的背景，
却没说成「操作系统」，主体被放大成笼统的「技术」，与原文具体所指不符。
D) 答非所问
An efficient person（高效的人）把主体说成人，对应的是首句对 multitasker 的「现
今」描述，而非题干要的「最初」所指，时间与主体都错。
