questions.stem: Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists?

options.label: A
options.text: They are not sufficiently exposed to multitasking situations.

options.label: B
options.text: They are not comparable to mechanical operating systems.

options.label: C
options.text: Their brains do not allow them to multitask.

options.label: D
options.text: Their attention span cannot be expanded.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】题干 Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists 问的是某方
观点下的具体理由，答案能在原文直接找到对应句。
【拆句】Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists：主干是 why ...
can't people be multitaskers（人为什么不能成为多任务者），really 加强语气，
according to neuroscientists 是状语，限定「按神经科学家的看法」。really 易让人误读
为「真的能吗」，其实它服务于全句的否定，意为「人确实当不了」。
【定位】So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not
handle multitasking situations well.
以至于，按照神经科学专家的说法，我们的大脑并不能很好地处理多任务情境。
【选项】A) 无中生有
not sufficiently exposed to multitasking situations（接触多任务情境不够）文中从
未提及，原文讲的是大脑机能，不是接触多少。
B) 答非所问
not comparable to mechanical operating systems（无法与机械操作系统相比）只是
首段把人和电脑作类比的延伸，并非神经科学家给出的不能多任务的理由。
C) ✓ 正确
our brains do not handle multitasking situations well ↔
Their brains do not allow them to multitask
预判的「大脑处理不好」与 Their brains do not allow them to multitask 一致，把原
因归于大脑这一生理层面，正合定位句。
D) 无中生有
attention span cannot be expanded（注意力广度无法扩展）文中并无此说，原文只
说两项任务争夺注意力时效率下降，没谈注意力能否扩展。
questions.locateHint: So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study on multitasking?

options.label: A
options.text: People make greater achievements by maintaining whatever they are doing is multitasking.

options.label: B
options.text: People's performance benefits from the perception of what they are doing as multitasking.

options.label: C
options.text: People's active mental processes exert a positive effect on their multitasking.

options.label: D
options.text: People can improve their capabilities by handling multitasking situations.

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题）
【判型】题干 What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study 问一项具体研究的结论，
原文有对应明示句，属可直接定位的细节。
【拆句】What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study on multitasking：主干 what
do we learn（我们了解到什么），from the conclusion of a recent study 是状语，on
multitasking 修饰 study，指「一项关于多任务的近期研究的结论」。结构平铺，无陷阱。
【定位】A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks
or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on
their performance.
一项近期研究得出结论：无论人们是否真的在处理多项任务，仅仅是他们把这一活动感知为
多任务这个事实，就对他们的表现有正面影响。
【选项】A) 偷换概念
maintaining whatever they are doing is multitasking 用 maintaining（坚持主张/坚
持做）替换原文的 perceive（感知），「坚称是多任务」不等于「感知为多任务」，把
主观认知偷换成口头主张。
B) ✓ 正确
they perceive this activity as multitasking ↔
the perception of what they are doing as multitasking
has a positive effect on their performance ↔ performance benefits from
预判的「感知为多任务即提升表现」与 People's performance benefits from the
perception of what they are doing as multitasking 完全对应，落点都在「感知」这
一主观因素。
C) 张冠李戴
active mental processes（积极的心理过程）借的是第二段讲切换需要不同 mental
processes 的内容，与本研究结论的「感知」无关。
D) 与原文相反
improve their capabilities by handling multitasking situations 说「靠处理多任务来
提升能力」，而原文强调的恰是「无论是否真在处理多任务」，重点在感知而非实际处
理，方向相反。
questions.locateHint: A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks

questions.stem: How does the business world view multitasking?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a rare skill often found in fluid organisations.

options.label: B
options.text: It is an adaptable capability required of all workers.

options.label: C
options.text: It is an essential quality many employees lack.

options.label: D
options.text: It is a desirable ability that can be developed.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题）
【判型】题干 How does the business world view multitasking 问商业界如何看待多任务，原文有
专段陈述该立场，属可定位细节。
【拆句】How does the business world view multitasking：view 在此是动词「看待」，主干为
the business world view multitasking（商业界如何看待多任务）。需注意 view 此处不是
名词「景观」而是动词，属熟词的常见用法。
【定位】From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be
taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their
working practices.
从这一不同视角看，你不仅可以做到多任务，而且这种能力还可以被传授：这在灵活的组织
里更容易做到，这类组织在工作方式上崇尚灵活性。
【选项】A) 与原文相反
a rare skill（罕见技能）与原文 many companies look for people who are skilled in
multitasking 矛盾——能被许多公司寻得且可传授，说明并不罕见。
B) 以偏概全
required of all workers（对所有员工的要求）把范围夸大成「全体员工」，原文只说
many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking，是企业青睐某些
人，而非要求所有人都具备。
C) 无中生有
many employees lack（许多员工缺乏）文中并无此说，原文谈的是公司想要、能力可
教，没有说员工普遍缺乏这种能力。
D) ✓ 正确
many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking ↔ a desirable ability
this ability can also be taught ↔ that can be developed
预判的「可培养的实用能力」与 a desirable ability that can be developed 两点全
中：desirable 对应被公司追求，can be developed 对应可教。

questions.stem: What does the author imply we should do if we have to focus on some task and do it well?
questions.explanation:
【答案】C （推断题）
【判型】题干 What does the author imply we should do 用 imply 问作者「暗示」我们该怎么
做，答案需基于原文推理而非直接摘录。
【拆句】What does the author imply we should do if we have to focus on some task and do
it well：主干 what does the author imply we should do（作者暗示我们该做什么），if
引导条件状语从句 if we have to focus on some task and do it well（如果我们必须专注
某项任务并把它做好）。从句是答案成立的前提，须连同主句一起理解。
【定位】But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration
are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.
但不得不同时关注好几件事，意味着专注力会下降，而这会导致更多错误。
【选项】A) 张冠李戴
Work in a flexible way（以灵活方式工作）取自第四段商业视角的 favour flexibility in
their working practices，与末段「要专注做好该怎么办」无关。
B) 无中生有
Learn from mistakes（从错误中学习）只是借了末段 mistakes 一词，原文说的是多任
务会「导致」更多错误，从未建议「从错误中学习」。
C) ✓ 正确
having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are
reduced
↔ Avoid multitasking
预判的「别同时做多件事」与 Avoid multitasking 一致——既然多任务降低专注、引发
错误，那要做好就该避免它。
D) 答非所问
Increase efficiency（提高效率）对应原文 Being quicker and more efficient，但那是
多任务的「好处」一面，并非「要专注做好」的对策；况且追求效率与多任务相伴，恰
是降低专注的根源。

title: 2023年12月真题·第1套 · 选词填空

paragraphs.text: Exercising for just 10 minutes a week is linked to a longer life, according to a new study published in The British Journal of Sports Medicine.

Several recent studies have found that even low-intensity exercise, done for a short amount of time, can have a meaningful  [26]  on health. Still, the idea that exercising for just 10 minutes a week may be enough to increase your lifespan is novel. It's also somewhat  [27]  , since the federal physical activity guidelines recommend getting at least 75 minutes of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes of  [28]  exercise each week.
The study was based on data from more than 88,000 U.S. adults who  [29]  in the National Health Interview Survey between 1997 and 2008.

Contrary to some research that has found an  [30]  limit to the amount of exercise that is healthy, the researchers found that there was  [31]  no limit to the longevity(长寿) benefits of exercise. Even the small group of people who got 10 times the amount of exercise recommended by the federal government had a 46% lower  [32]  of death than the least active group.

Still, observational studies like this one cannot prove cause and effect; they can only find  [33]  . The researchers also were not able to  [34]  for certain lifestyle factors that could affect lifespan, including dietary habits and changes in physical activity over time. Despite these  [35]  , the study's results are yet another indication of the power of physical activity, even in small amounts.

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】F) impact
名词
【词性槽】形容词 meaningful 后、a 后缺名词
【依据】have an impact on 是固定搭配，意为"对……产生影响"
even low-intensity exercise, done for a short amount of time, can have a meaningful
__(26)__ on health——have a(n) impact on health 即"对健康有影响"，搭配标准、语义
贴切：低强度运动对健康有切实影响，正是本段要点。
【竞争词】N) type type 不搭 meaningful…on，语义也不通
a meaningful type on health（"对健康的一种有意义的类型"）讲不通，type 也不与 on 构
成"对……的"含义；这里要表达的是运动对健康的"作用/影响"。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】D) controversial
形容词
【词性槽】系动词 is + somewhat 之后作表语，需形容词
【依据】因与官方指南冲突，故"有争议"
It's also somewhat __(27)__, since the federal physical activity guidelines recommend
getting at least 75 minutes of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes of __(28)__ exercise
——since 给出理由："10分钟即可"的说法和官方推荐的几十上百分钟相去甚远，自然"有些
争议"。controversial 与这层让步/对立逻辑严丝合缝。
【竞争词】H) moderate moderate 义为"适度的"，与 since 的争议逻辑不合，且它另有归宿
moderate 表"中等/适度"，无法解释"because 它和官方指南相左"这层因果；况且 moderate
更贴 28 空的 moderate exercise（适度运动）固定搭配，应留给 28 题。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】H) moderate
形容词
【词性槽】名词 exercise 前作定语，需形容词
【依据】与 vigorous 对照，moderate exercise 即"适度/中等强度运动"
at least 75 minutes of vigorous exercise or 150 minutes of __(28)__ exercise——
vigorous（剧烈）对应 75 分钟，or 后强度更低的运动要更多时长 150 分钟，正是
moderate（中等强度）。moderate exercise 是健康指南里的固定表达，与 vigorous 形
成强度对照。
【竞争词】O) upper upper 不修饰运动强度，且它另有归宿
upper 意为"上面的/上限的"，不能说 upper exercise；况且 upper 更贴 30 空的 upper limit
（上限）固定搭配，应留给 30 题。这里要的是与 vigorous 对照的强度词。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】I) participated
动词
【词性槽】关系代词 who 后缺谓语，要填动词且用过去式
【依据】participate in 是固定搭配，意为"参与某调查"
空后紧跟 in：who __(29)__ in the National Health Interview Survey，participate in 正
是"参加（一项调查/活动）"的标准搭配，主语是 88,000 名成年人，语义完全契合"参加了
全国健康访谈调查"。
【竞争词】A) adjust 搭配与语义都不对
adjust 意为"调整"，常搭 adjust for/to，不能说"人 adjust in 一项调查"，语义上成年人"调整进
调查"也讲不通。
B) alter 义为"改变"，与"参加调查"无关
alter 是"改动、改变"，"成年人改变了这项调查"既不合常理也不搭 in，与上下文的研究取样语境
冲突。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】O) upper
形容词
【词性槽】名词 limit 前、an 后作定语，需形容词
【依据】upper limit（上限）是固定搭配，呼应"运动量过多是否仍健康"
Contrary to some research that has found an __(30)__ limit to the amount of exercise
that is healthy——upper limit 即"上限"：有研究认为健康运动量存在一个上限，而本研究
发现"几乎没有上限"，前后正成对比，upper limit 搭配地道、逻辑契合。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】M) seemingly
副词
【词性槽】修饰 no limit 的程度/口吻，需副词
【依据】对"无上限"这一惊人结论留有余地，"看似"无上限
there was __(31)__ no limit to the longevity benefits of exercise——"运动延寿几乎没
有上限"是个强结论，作者用 seemingly（看似、貌似）留有余地，既转述发现又不把话说
满，符合科普文严谨口吻。
【竞争词】C) approximately approximately 修饰数字，不修饰"no limit"
approximately"大约"通常修饰具体数量（approximately 75 minutes），用来修饰"no
limit"这种非数值判断不通顺；这里要的是表"看似"的语气副词，而非约数副词。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 C) —— approximately 词性也对，易与 seemingly 混淆。两者都
是副词，there was __(31)__ no limit，考生可能想"approximately no limit（大约没上
限）"；但 approximately 只修饰数字，修饰"no limit"这种结论不通。防坑：先问空修饰
的是数字还是判断，约数副词只贴数字。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】L) risk
名词
【词性槽】形容词 lower 之后、of death 之前缺名词
【依据】risk of death（死亡风险）是固定搭配，且呼应"延寿"主题
had a 46% lower __(32)__ of death——risk of death 即"死亡风险"，运动多的人死亡风
险低 46%，正好支撑全文"运动有益寿命"的主旨，搭配与语义双双契合。
【竞争词】N) type type of death 不合此处逻辑
type of death 是"死亡的类型"，无法用"lower"来比较高低，也和"运动延寿、降低死亡可能"的
语境对不上；这里要的是可量化升降的"风险"。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】J) patterns
名词
【词性槽】动词 find 后缺宾语，需复数名词
【依据】与"不能证因果、只能发现关联"形成对照，patterns 即"关联型态"
observational studies like this one cannot prove cause and effect; they can only find
__(33)__——分号前后是对比：不能证明因果，只能找出"模式/关联"。patterns 正指观察研
究能看到的相关规律，与 cause and effect 恰成对照。
【竞争词】E) coordinates 义为"坐标"，与研究方法语境无关
coordinates 多指数学"坐标"，放进"观察研究只能发现什么"的语境毫无意义，与 cause and
effect 的对照逻辑也搭不上。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】A) adjust
动词
【词性槽】情态 able to 之后缺动词原形
【依据】adjust for 是研究术语，意为"校正、排除……因素的影响"
were not able to __(34)__ for certain lifestyle factors that could affect lifespan——
adjust for（在统计中）"对某些因素加以校正/控制"是研究方法的固定说法，承接上文"该研
究有局限"：研究者没能排除饮食、运动量变化等干扰因素，逻辑严丝合缝。
【竞争词】B) alter alter 不搭 for，且语义相反
alter 是"改变"，常作及物动词（alter something），不与 for 构成"校正"义；说"研究者没能改
变这些因素"不合科研语境，这里要的是"校正/控制"而非"改变"。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 B) —— alter 与 adjust 同为"改变"义动词，极易误选。两词都是动
词、词义都沾"改动"，考生易凭眼熟选 alter；但本句要的是科研术语 adjust for（校正/排
除因素），alter 既不搭 for 又语义偏"改变"。防坑：动词空务必把空后的介词（for）和候
选连读，搭不通的立刻淘汰。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】G) limitations
名词
【词性槽】介词 Despite + these 之后缺名词，且要复数
【依据】承接上文研究的两处不足，these 指代"这些局限"
上文刚说研究 cannot prove cause and effect 又 were not able to __(34)__ for certain
lifestyle factors，这些都是研究的不足；Despite these limitations（尽管有这些局限）正
好回指这两处缺陷，转折后再肯定研究价值，逻辑顺畅。
【竞争词】J) patterns 义为"模式"，指代不上前文的"缺陷"
patterns 是"模式、规律"，前文讲的是研究做不到什么（局限），不是某种模式；说"尽管有这
些模式"与上下文转折逻辑不符。

title: 2023年12月真题·第1套 · 长篇匹配（How Climate Change Will ）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct(灭绝的) due to climate change. Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. By using the genes from resurrection(复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. Despite alarmist headlines about "foods that are going extinct," there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food. We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. "Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the US Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office. In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30℃ is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean(大豆) production in the US show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold(临界点).

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: In the US—the world's largest producer of corn and soybeans—farms can move north to some degree, Schlenker says. But eventually, yields will likely suffer because the soil north of Iowa declines in quality—a legacy of glacial(冰川的) expansion. Other studies, including studies of wheat in India and corn in Africa, also found that there is a threshold above which yields sharply decline: crops can adapt and move, but only to a point. "What's common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop," Schlenker says. "If predictions for the end of the century are true, though, I think a lot of agricultural areas in the US will see significant hits."

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Under current conditions, about 4% of the world's croplands experience drought in any given year, but by the end of the century those conditions are forecasted to jump to about 18% per year. Some studies indicate that horticulture crops—generally, everything besides staples—may be impacted most severely, largely because they tend to be confined to a smaller geographic area. Researcher Andrew Jarvis and his colleagues found that 80% of coffee-growing zones in Central America and Brazil could become unsuitable by 2050, for example, while climate change will likely have "great impacts" on cocoa(可可粉) production in West Africa. "High quality chocolate will be less available in the future, and if you want it, you'll have to pay a lot more for it," Jarvis says.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: This means that, for those who can afford it, some foods will simply cost them more in the future. But for poorer people, those same price jumps will likely cause certain foods to go extinct from their diets. "The more you reduce, the shorter the supply, and the higher the price will jump," Schlenker says.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Another potential climate change-induced problem is our dependence on commodity crops—wheat, soybeans, corn and rice—which currently provide humanity with 75% of its calories, either directly or indirectly through the animals we raise on those crops. Jarvis and his colleagues also found that, over the past five decades, the world has seen an increasing standardisation of diets; the foods we eat globally today are 36% more similar than they were in 1961. While this can be good news for the world's poorest people who now consume more calories, protein and fat than in the past, homogeneity(同一性) and over-dependence on a handful of staples leave us vulnerable to threats such as drought, disease and pests—all of which are predicted to worsen in many parts of the world as a result of climate change.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: There are ways we could soften the coming blow to the global food supply, however. Like Farrant's work with resurrection crops, a number of companies, organisations and researchers are aiming to create drought and temperature-resistant crops through genetic engineering and conventional breeding. For now, the jury is still out as to how successful those endeavours will be. "The people at Monsanto who I've talked to are much more optimistic that they'll be able to engineer heat-tolerant crops," Schlenker says. "On the other hand, scientists at the USDA who I've spoken with are much more cautious."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Until genetic engineering comes to fruition, other strategies might also help in some places, including applying more fertiliser, implementing better irrigation, using machinery that gets crops out of the field faster or installing storage facilities to delay spoilage. "Many places could benefit a great deal just by using technologies that already exist," Walsh says. "General farm management can go a long way toward easing changes."

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Finally, diversifying our diet away from heat-sensitive wheat, corn, rice and other crops could also help. "We've seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue," M Jarvis says. "Depending on a greater number of plant species creates a more vigorous and less risky food system—and one that provides a broader range of nutritional requirements."

title: 2023年12月真题·第1套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: One of my bad habits is saying "busy" when people ask me how I'm doing. Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. But working long hours doesn't drive better results. Never taking a vacation won't lead to a promotion. So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time?

In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility. In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing.

That's why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there's a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress, then they're probably a big deal. This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout(精疲力竭).

Personally, I'm going to stop saying "busy" when people ask me how I am. It sounds self-righteous(自以为是的) and sets the wrong tone. Phrases like "I have limited access to email" and "I'll respond as soon as I get back" sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off.

That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same.

title: 2023年12月真题·第1套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: Female employees consistently pay lower airfares than men do for the same flights because they tend to book earlier.

We compared the airfare paid by employees in the same position within a company for the same class of travel and used a common statistical technique to account for other factors that might affect differences in airfares. We found that women paid on average $18 less per ticket than their male colleagues. Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average.

We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late. None of these explained away the gender gap, so we applied data collected from surveys that express consumer preferences that play a central role in economic decisions, such as patience and risk avoidance.

We found that only the concept of "negative reciprocity"—in which an employee who feels unfairly treated engages in negative behaviors, such as spending their company's money less carefully—explains these differences. The surveys showed men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women. This isn't to say that all men engage in these behaviors—or that booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior. It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable.
Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale(士气) and culture.
Our results show another way these negative behaviors can manifest themselves, like in airline bookings, and add to evidence that women are less likely to engage in them.

Companies spend significant sums of money on business travel. While that $18 difference per ticket may seem small, it adds up. Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers.

C) 偷换概念
原文成因是订得早晚，并非男性“更愿意多付钱”；male employees' readiness to pay

title: 2023年06月真题·第3套 · 长篇匹配（A Club Where Lions Dance）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The first thing you notice in the staircase to the fourth-floor studio on Canal Street in Manhattan, New York, is the measured thumping(嘭嘭声) coming from behind a metal door. Just beyond the entrance, large lion masks were twisting and turning to the drum-beat. On a recent Friday evening, the teenagers made their way across the studio floor as they practiced Chinese lion dancing.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: "You want to play in a circle," Victor Fong, aged 24, told his students at the New York Chinese Freemasons Athletic Club. "Take it slow and do it again." The dance group, made up of 60 members, performs throughout the year but was now preparing for its biggest events, Chinese Lunar New Year celebrations, which will begin on Saturday and conclude on February 15. Teenagers comprise about half of the group, many of whom began lion dancing at the age of 14. About 100 current and past members of the dance group—which has been performing since 1956—will be among the 220 groups marching through Chinatown in Manhattan for the 18th Lunar New Year Parade on February 5.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Mr. Fong has been involved in the organization since he was 15 and began teaching lion dancing three years ago. But the club also acts as a recreation center and safe haven(庇护所) for teenagers, with video games readily available. As many as 20 students show up after school. "The basic requirement for hanging out here is you have to learn how to lion dance," Mr. Fong said. While that is not a formal requirement for being a member, everyone finds a way to participate in the Lunar New Year Parade, whether it's by dancing, carrying a flag or beating a drum.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Alvin Chau, aged 26, is an environmental consultant by day and a lion dancer on weekends. He has been a club member for 10 years and joined because of an interest in lion dance. "We're a big family," he said, shaking hands with other members as they walked through the door. "You know everyone."

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: It is believed that the lion dance began in the third century. Stories vary about how lion dancing came to be, but most of them include a monster named Nian who would terrorize a village. The villagers finally banded together and scared the beast away with firecrackers(爆竹) and drums. While lions are not native to China, some versions of the story include the villagers creating a monster of their own in the shape of a lion to fight off the beast.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Today, the dancers travel across Chinatown going from business to business to bring good luck for the coming year. The new year—according to the Chinese lunar calendar—will begin on Saturday and marks the Year of the Rooster(鸡年), which is thought to be a symbol of positivity. "It's almost like the dark night is ending and the sun is coming up," said Ya Yung Teng, the digital collections coordinator for the Museum of Chinese in America. "It's hopeful that we're going to have a new day." Roosters and chickens are not particularly strong creatures, Ms. Teng said, but they are numerous. "In a way," she said, the rooster "stands for 'We the People.'"

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The lion head and tail are operated by two people. As one person controls the head, a second follows under a train of fabric representing the body. The dancers move in harmony as they imitate the animal's natural movements in the wild, including the aggressiveness of an attack. A lion head figure weighs under 10 pounds and sits squarely on the dancer's shoulders. Inside, the dancer manipulates strings that open and close the lion's eyes, shake its ears and open its mouth to reveal a fire-orange tongue.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: "A good lion dancer will imitate a living creature," said Karlin Chan, aged 59, who heads the athletic club's community public relations. "I started lion dancing when I was a kid," he said. "Chinatown was much smaller then and it was a celebration with fireworks and firecrackers, which added a lot of flavor and meaning to it."

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Mr. Chan buys a new lion head each year when he travels to China. A head costs about $1,500. "If you want the good stuff, the quality, you have to see it for yourself," he said. "I'll inspect the product before we put it in the container and ship it over." Mr. Chan, who has been involved with the club for nearly 50 years, said that passing the dance from one generation to the next was vital. "You need to pass on the traditions and the culture, and this is a part of our culture," he said. "It's a great way to promote cultural understanding and exchange; we welcome that."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: For Sara Pore, aged 17, another club member, lion dance is more than just tradition; it provides a creative outlet. "Lion dancing started 2,000 years ago—that's incredible," she said. "But what makes you a competent lion dancer is that there's a sense of imagination involved. Lion dancing teaches competence in leadership because of this. You're constantly forced to push yourself past your limit."

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Back at rehearsal(排练), Just in Le, aged 18, tied a red ribbon around his waist to practice jumping. The dancers use the ribbons to pull themselves up over their partners' heads. The room's ceilings are too low to wear the lion heads for jumping practice, so once up on his partner's head, Mr. Le held out his arms as if in offering.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Mr. Le comes by the dance as a legacy(传承). "I was born into it," Mr. Le said, noting that his uncle and father were club members. "Growing up, I would always watch my family and see the lion dance, and I slowly grew interested in it." By the age of 14, he was fully enrolled in the athletic club's lion dance group. "I value my culture and tradition, being Chinese or Asian-American. I have a lot of pride in that," he said. "I want to contribute and give back to the community."

title: 2023年06月真题·第3套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: Team-building exercises have become popular for managers trying to increase organisational and team harmony and productivity. Unfortunately many employees resent compulsory bonding and often regard these exercises as a nuisance.

A paper published this week by University of Sydney researchers in Social Networks has reported participants' feelings about team-building interventions(干预), revealing ethical implications in forcing employees to take part.
"Many people see team-building activities as a waste of time, so we decided to look in more depth at what's behind this," said the paper's lead researcher, Dr. Peter Matous.

"Teams are formed, combined and restructured. Staff are relocated and office spaces redesigned. All this is done with the aim of improving workplace efficiency, collaboration and cohesion. But does any of this work?" said Dr. Matous.

The study found that team-building exercises which focused on the sharing of and intervening into personal attitudes and relationships between team members were considered too heavy-handed and intrusive, although the researchers say some degree of openness and vulnerability is often necessary to make deep, effective connections with colleagues.

"Some participants were against team-building exercises because they were implicitly compulsory. They didn't welcome management's interest in their lives beyond their direct work performance," said Matous. "Many people don't want to be forced into having fun or making friends, especially not on top of their busy jobs. They feel management is being too nosy or trying to control their lives too much."

In this study the researchers recommended a self-disclosure(表露) approach where participants were guided through a series of questions that allowed them to increasingly disclose personal information and values. The method is well-tested and has been shown to increase interpersonal closeness. However, to be successful it must be voluntary.

The researchers said there are numerous schools of thought that propose differing psychological methods for strengthening relationships. "With caution, many relational methods to improve teams and organisations can be borrowed from other fields. The question is how to apply them effectively to strengthen an entire collective, which is more than just the sum of individual relationships," said Dr. Matous.

title: 2023年06月真题·第3套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 2

paragraphs.text: There are close to 58,000 homeless people in Los Angeles county. That's a shocking and tragic number for a region that's home to some of the richest people in the world. At last, the problem became so acute—and so visible—that Los Angeles took extraordinary action. The citizens of this county voted in November 2016 and again in March 2017 to raise their own taxes. The purpose of such action is to fund an enormous multibillion-dollar, 10-year program of housing and social services for the homeless.

As a result, Los Angeles now has its best chance in decades to combat homelessness. This is an opportunity that surely all can agree must not be wasted. It is neither desirable nor morally acceptable nor practical for this county to tolerate the signs of deprivation more commonly associated with the slums(贫民窟) of Rio de Janiero.

How did we get here? For as long as there are homeless people, there is a tendency to blame the victims themselves for their condition—to see their failure to thrive as an issue of character, of moral weakness, of laziness. But contrary to popular belief, the homeless in Los Angeles are not mostly mentally ill or drug addicted or frightening, although a sizable minority meet some of those descriptions. Today, a greater and greater proportion of people living on the streets are there because of bad luck or a series of mistakes, or because the economy forgot them—they lost a job or were evicted(逐出) or fled an abusive marriage just as the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving.

The challenges are enormous, even if everyone is pulling in the same direction. That reality was driven home this month by a new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report showing that the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing.

In the world's richest nation, homelessness on this scale should be shameful and shocking. But most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed. Increasingly, we are uncomfortable, annoyed, disgusted, scared or unaware. Compassion(同情心) is being replaced by resignation.

The Noor solar power station is  [26]  in the city of Ouarzazate and, once completed, will generate 580 million watts of electricity. The World Bank estimates it will serve 1.1 million people. It's  [27]  to be completed soon.

Morocco's current energy comes  [28]  from imports. The nation hopes to get 50 percent of its energy from renewable sources by 2030. With demand for energy  [29]  at an annual rate of 7 percent, the new solar plant could be a  [30]  part of that goal.

"This makes Morocco a big  [31]  in the field of solar energy in the Arab region and the African continent. It could also be a forerunner for many other countries in the world that  [32]  on foreign imports of energy," said Ali Hajji, a solar energy specialist and engineering professor.

Experts believe that the Middle East and North Africa have huge  [33]  for solar energy projects. This is partly because of adequate sunlight and partly because technology has become more  [34]  in the region.
"The last few years have seen a realization of  [35]  how competitive solar technologies can be," said Michael Taylor, a senior analyst at the International Renewable Energy Agency.

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】H) located
动词
【词性槽】be 动词 is 后缺成分，构成被动 be + 过去分词
【依据】be located in 是'位于'的固定表达
located 与空后的 in the city 构成 be located in（位于某地），正好回答'电站在哪
里'，语义和搭配双双吻合：The Noor solar power station is __(26)__ in the city
of Ouarzazate。
【竞争词】D) depend 搭配错，depend 配 on 不配 in
depend 表'依赖'要搭 depend on，且'电站依赖某城市'语义不通，与空后 in 也不搭。
F) insist 语义不通，电站不会'坚持'
insist 是'坚持主张'，主语须是人或机构，'电站坚持于某城'完全讲不通。
J) operating 时态/语态不对，主动进行不合句意
is operating 是'正在运转'，但下文 once completed, will generate 表明电站尚未建成，谈不
上正在运转，逻辑冲突。
O) scheduled 搭配错，scheduled 配 to 不配 in
be scheduled 后通常接 to do（预定要做某事），接 in + 地点表'位于'不成立；它真正的归宿
是 27 空。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】O) scheduled
动词
【词性槽】It's + 空 + to be → be + 过去分词 + 不定式
【依据】be scheduled to do = 预定要做某事
It's __(27)__ to be completed soon. → It's scheduled to be completed soon，'它预定
将很快完工'，be scheduled to do 是固定搭配，正好衔接前句 once completed, will
generate（一旦建成就发电）所暗示的'尚未完工但即将完工'。
【竞争词】D) depend 搭配错，depend 配 on 不接 to be done
depend 要搭 depend on，'它依赖被完成'语义和搭配都不成立。
F) insist 主语是物，不能'坚持'
insist 主语须为人/机构，且无 be insisted to do 这种用法，电站不会'坚持要被完成'。
J) operating is operating to be 句型不成立
operating 是现在分词，is operating to be completed 句型讲不通，逻辑上电站也尚未运转。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】I) mostly
副词
【词性槽】comes 与 from 之间缺修饰 → 副词
【依据】mostly = 主要地，呼应下句50%目标
Morocco's current energy comes __(28)__ from imports. 说现状'主要靠进口'，正好与下
句 The nation hopes to get 50 percent of its energy from renewable sources by
2030. 形成'现在主要进口、将来转向可再生'的对照，mostly（主要地）语义最贴。
【竞争词】G) just just 在此偏'仅仅'，与下文规模矛盾
just 作副词常表'仅仅'，'仅仅来自进口'语气偏轻，且 just 真正的归宿是 35 空的 just how（到
底多么）固定语境。
K) perhaps perhaps 表推测，与陈述事实冲突
perhaps 是'也许'，但本句在陈述当前能源结构的客观事实，不是猜测，用'也许来自进口'语气
不对。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】N) rising
形容词
【词性槽】with + 名词 + 空，作 demand 的状态修饰
【依据】rising 配 at a rate of 7% 表'以7%速率增长'
With demand for energy __(29)__ at an annual rate of 7 percent，demand rising at a
rate of 7 percent 即'需求以每年 7%的速率增长'，rising（上升的）与后面的'年增长率'数
据精确呼应。
【竞争词】A) affordable 义不搭，需求无所谓'负担得起'
affordable 指价格可负担，修饰商品/价格，不能说'需求是负担得起的'，且与 at a rate 不搭。
C) crucial 义不搭，且不能接 at a rate
crucial 是'至关重要的'，'需求至关重要地以 7%'读不通；它真正的归宿是 30 空。
E) initial initial 表'最初的'，与'年增长率'无关
initial 指'起初的、最初阶段的'，无法描述一个持续的增长速率，语义与 at an annual rate
冲突。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】C) crucial
形容词
【词性槽】a + 空 + part → 名词前定语 → 形容词
【依据】crucial part = 关键的一环，褒义贴目标
the new solar plant could be a __(30)__ part of that goal，承接前句'2030 年要 50%靠
可再生'的宏大目标，新电站是实现该目标'至关重要的一环'，crucial（关键的）感情色彩与
分量都吻合。
【竞争词】E) initial initial 表'最初的'，与'实现目标的关键'错位
initial part 是'最初的部分/起步阶段'，但文意强调电站对达成目标的'重要性'，不是强调它是'第
一步'，语义指向不同，分量也偏弱。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 E) —— initial 词性也对、'最初的一环'也通。a __(30)__ part of
that goal 填 initial 语法毫无破绽，'最初的部分'听着也合理；但全文强调新电站对达成
50%可再生目标的'关键作用'，强调重要性而非时间先后，故选 crucial。防坑：近义形容词
二选一时，回原文确认作者到底在强调'重要'还是'最初'。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】L) pioneer
名词
【词性槽】a + 空（+介词短语）作表语 → 名词
【依据】pioneer = 先锋，褒义且呼应'forerunner'
This makes Morocco a big __(31)__ in the field of solar energy in the Arab
region，'使摩洛哥成为太阳能领域的一大先锋'，pioneer（先锋/开拓者）褒义贴切，并与
同段 It could also be a forerunner for many other countries（先行者）同义呼应，是命
题人埋的同义线索。
【竞争词】B) ancestor ancestor 指'祖先'，用于人/血统不用于领域
ancestor 是'祖先、先辈'，指血缘世系，不能说一个国家是某领域的'祖先'，与 in the field of
solar energy 搭不上。
M) potential potential 在此句作名词指'潜力'，语义错位
a big potential 是'巨大潜力'，但本句说摩洛哥已经'成为'领域里的角色（make...a big ___），
需要的是'角色身份'类名词而非'潜力'；potential 该用在 33 空。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】D) depend
动词
【词性槽】关系词 that 后缺谓语 → 动词
【依据】depend on foreign imports = 依赖外国进口
countries in the world that __(32)__ on foreign imports of energy，depend on（依
赖）正配空后的 on，'依赖能源外国进口的国家'语义通顺，且呼应前文 Morocco's current
energy comes __(28)__ from imports. 的'靠进口'主线。
【竞争词】F) insist insist on 义为'坚持主张'，逻辑不合
insist on 虽也搭 on，但义为'坚决主张做某事'，'坚持外国能源进口'不合此处'依赖进口'的语境
逻辑。
J) operating 形态不对，从句需原形谓语
operating 是分词，不能直接作 that 从句的谓语（缺助动词），且 operate on 语义也不通。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 F) —— insist on 搭配看着也成立。that __(32)__ on foreign
imports of energy 里 insist on 与 depend on 都能搭 on，最易误选；但'坚持外国进口'不
合'依赖进口'的文意。防坑：搭配相同就比谁的词义贴上下文逻辑，依赖（depend）才是本
篇主线。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】M) potential
名词
【词性槽】have huge + 空 → 形容词后名词中心词
【依据】huge potential for = 巨大潜力，搭配天成
the Middle East and North Africa have huge __(33)__ for solar energy projects，have
huge potential for（在……方面有巨大潜力）是地道搭配，'中东北非太阳能项目潜力巨
大'语义通顺，正承接下句讲的'阳光充足、技术更便宜'两大有利条件。
【竞争词】B) ancestor ancestor 指'祖先'，与'地区有潜力'毫不相干
ancestor 是血缘'祖先'，'地区有巨大祖先'完全讲不通，且无 have ancestor for 用法。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】A) affordable
形容词
【词性槽】become more 后接空 → 形容词比较级中心词
【依据】技术变得更'便宜'才会被推广
本段讲该地区适合太阳能的原因，partly because of adequate sunlight and partly
because technology has become more __(34)__ in the region。技术'变得更负担得起
（成本更低）'正是推动太阳能项目的合理原因，affordable 语义最贴；这也与下段 how
competitive solar technologies can be（太阳能技术多有竞争力）相呼应。
【竞争词】C) crucial crucial 不能比较成'更关键'修饰技术成本
'技术变得更至关重要'读着别扭，且本句因果是'技术更便宜→项目更可行'，crucial 不切此因
果；它该用在 30 空。
E) initial initial 表'最初的'，无比较级语义
initial 指'最初阶段的'，本身不表程度，说'技术变得更最初的'逻辑不通。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】G) just
副词
【词性槽】空 + how + 形容词 → 修饰整个感叹/疑问短语
【依据】just how... = '到底多么……'，加强语气
a realization of __(35)__ how competitive solar technologies can be → just how
competitive，just 在 how 前作'究竟、到底'解，强调'人们意识到太阳能技术到底有多大竞
争力'，语气贴合专家感叹的口吻。
【竞争词】K) perhaps perhaps 表猜测，与'已意识到'矛盾
perhaps 是'也许'，但句子说 a realization of...（已经意识到了），是确定的认知而非猜测，'也
许多么有竞争力'语气自相矛盾，且 perhaps 不与 how 连用作此加强义。

title: 2023年06月真题·第2套 · 长篇匹配（New Formula One Chief Ho）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: For the past four decades, the leader of Formula One car racing, one of the biggest annual sporting series in the world, was Bernie Ecclestone, a former motorcycle parts dealer who built it into an international presence essentially on his own.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: A skilled backroom operator who speaks without a filter, Ecclestone said often that in his opinion, the sport was at its best when he was allowed to act as "a dictator."

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Yet now the dictator is gone. After an American company, Liberty Media, acquired the Formula One competition recently, Chase Carey—a former executive with Fox Broadcasting Company and DirecTV who by his own admission is not a fierce racing fan—was named to replace Ecclestone and to try to renovate the organization's management, reach and ambition.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Among the goals, Carey said in an interview on Tuesday, is one that just about every global sport seems interested in chasing: increasing interest in the United States. "People have said we're going to 'Americanize' it," Carey said. "And we're not going to do that totally. But realistically, there are some elements of Americanization that the sport could use."

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: While Formula One commands enormous audiences throughout much of the world, many American sports fans know it as that other motorsport, the one that is not Nascar(纳斯卡车赛). Formula One teams race far more technologically advanced vehicles around tracks all over the world—in magnificent events in places like Malaysia, Monaco, Singapore and the United Arab Emirates, and on tradition-rich tracks like Silverstone in England and Monza in Italy too.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The series has an annual race in Austin, Texas. But within "a few years," Carey said, he plans to bring another to a destination American city, like New York, Los Angeles, Miami or Las Vegas. Carey's ambitious plan is two-fold: first, change the business model of Formula One, which he said was a "one-man show" under Ecclestone that had a largely narrow vision when it came to negotiating partnership deals; and second, alter the way fans experience the sport, both in person and remotely, so that connections between the audience and people within the series are easier to make.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Increased digital access for fans, a more behind-the-scenes experience for broadcast viewers and innovation in areas like virtual reality—what is it like to speed around a track inside a Ferrari?—are among the possibilities. "The sport has clearly been underserved," Carey said. "It doesn't do anything digitally. There's no marketing. It doesn't tell any stories. The goal in this is to make the fans connect to the live experience as much as possible, and the tools you have to do that, we're not using at all."

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The larger question, though, is a familiar one: Is there room for Formula One in the ever-crowded sports landscape of the United States? Opinions vary, particularly because viewing habits among consumers continue to evolve. John Bloom, a professor at Shippensburg University who has studied American sports history, said the biggest challenge for any sport trying to increase its presence in the United States was framing itself in a way that had lasting appeal. "Sports generally become popular in some way because they establish a narrative," Bloom said. "When I think of motorsports in the U.S., what we all think of is Nascar, and the narrative of Nascar is sort of rural, white, working-class Americans, mostly in the South, connecting with the atmosphere of those races. That's the narrative. When I think of the narrative of Formula One, it's a very different kind of audience."

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: That difference, Carey said, is significant. While some might immediately link Formula One to Nascar in terms of American growth, Carey said Formula One's brand research had indicated there was very little crossover; rather, Formula One fans generally cite other so-called elite events, like Wimbledon or the Ryder Cup, as competitions they enjoy. "Other than they're both cars, the Nascar fan base is a very different fan base," Carey said. "It's a very regional fan base. Formula One is a global, famous brand of stars. These are machines that shock and awe you."

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Carey's background is in deal making and innovation. At Fox Broadcasting Company, he was a top advisor for years, known for his skill in helping to lead the launch of the company into sports, as well as the start of Fox News Channel. After going to DirecTV, he positioned the satellite provider as a mainstream option in millions of households.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: Now, after Liberty Media paid $4.4 billion to acquire Formula One, he is charged with making the investment pay off. "I think they can build Formula One in the U.S.," said Patrick Crakes, an executive at InVivo Media Group who spent 25 years at Fox Broadcasting Company before leaving in 2016 as a senior manager at Fox Sports. "People don't work on their cars anymore. They don't want that connection anymore. It's about technology and pushing the limits. It's about speed, danger and risk. And Formula One has that more than any other racing series."

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: That is what hooked Carey, and he said he thought his experience was not unusual. He recalled attending Formula One's Monaco race last year and being overwhelmed by the ceremony leading up to the event, the way the race charmed the city for days ahead of the start. In his mind, it felt like a Super Bowl(超级碗橄榄球赛).

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Then, on race day, he watched as the cars rocketed out of a tunnel and went screaming toward a tight turn with the city's harbor and the Mediterranean Sea in the background framing the scene. He was fascinated. "You can't help but be awed," he said, "and I think that feeling can be translated to the viewer."

paragraphs.label: N
paragraphs.text: He added: "The broader sport is a little too inward-looking, and we need to be more open. In some ways, I'm glad to be coming from the outside. The guys who are in the sport forever are sitting there saying: 'We can't do that. We can't do that because it's never been done that way.'"

paragraphs.text: Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change.

Supermarkets can technically be defined as giants housing 15,000 to 60,000 different products. The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America. There is some debate about which was the very first, but over the years a consensus has built around King Kullen Supermarket, founded in New York in 1930.

For some 300 years, Americans had fed themselves from small stores and public markets. Shopping for food involved mud, noisy chickens, clouds of flies, nasty smells, bargaining, and getting short-changed. The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food. Supermarkets may not feel cutting-edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time. They were such strange marvels that, on her first official state visit to the United States in 1957, Queen Elizabeth II insisted on an impromptu(即兴的) tour of a suburban-Maryland Giant Food.

The typical supermarket layout has barely changed over the past 90 years. Most stores open with flowers, fruit and vegetables at the front as a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite. Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you'll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way.

In the early days, as the supermarket multiplied, so did our suspicion of it. We have long feared that this "revolution in distribution" uses corporate black magic on our appetite. The book The Hidden Persuaders, published in 1957, warned that supermarkets were putting women in a "hypnoidal trance(催眠恍惚状态)," causing them to wander aisles bumping into boxes and "picking things off shelves at random."

options.label: C

【拆句】What problem have supermarkets been facing? 是一个 what 引导的特殊疑问句，主干
是"超市一直在面对什么难处"，have been facing 是现在完成进行时，强调"长期、持续"在
面对，这个时态暗示原文会有 long/for more than a decade 一类的长期信号词，结构本
身无陷阱。
【定位】Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in
existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. For more than a
decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans
fat, and accused of contributing to climate change.
长期以来，超市一直是利润最薄的行业之一，也是人们最不愿去工作或光顾的场所之一。十
多年来，它们一直受到电商巨头的攻击，被指责让美国人发胖，还被指控加剧气候变化。
【选项】A) 过度推断
原文只说超市利润薄、处境难，从未说它"正走向破产"；on the way to bankruptcy
把"利润薄"夸大成"濒临破产"，程度严重超出原文。
B) ✓ 正确
thinnest-margined businesses ↔ losing customers and profits
under attack from e-commerce giants ↔ losing customers

customers and profits. 同时覆盖了原文的"利润薄"和"受电商攻击"，与预判最契合。
C) 偷换概念
原文说超市"受电商攻击"，并没说它们"被迫去采用电商策略"；forced to use e-
commerce strategies 把"被攻击"偷换成"被迫效仿"，是原文未提的内容。

原文是超市"被指责加剧气候变化"（超市是被指责方），而 have difficulty adapting to
climate change 说成"超市难以适应气候变化"，把"被指责制造问题"换成了"自己适应
不了"。

paragraphs.text: The traditional school year, with three months of vacation every summer, was first implemented when America was an agricultural society and the summer months were needed for farm work. Since then, we've completely changed as a nation. Students no longer spend summers farming, but they aren't in school, either. The average American student receives 13 weeks off from school each calendar year-with about 11 of those during the summer. Few other countries have more than seven weeks off in a school calendar.

With the U.S. lagging behind other countries in academics, it's time to consider year-round schooling. One benefit of this change is that students will not fall victim to the "summer slide," or the well-documented phenomenon where students forget some of the knowledge they have acquired when too much time is taken off from school. Decades of research shows that it can take from 8 to 13 weeks at the beginning of every school year for students to get back to where they were before the summer holiday.

But year-round schooling isn't just about academics. Teachers and students experience a closer relationship in year-round schools than they do in traditional schools and, in the absence of any long-term break, students do not feel detached from the school environment. These closer bonds and greater attachment pay off. Research shows that students in year-round schools are more self-confident and feel more positive about their schooling experience.

But don't kids need time to relax? Some childhood development experts believe that time off from school is vital to healthy development as kids are not designed to spend so much of their time inside classrooms and the summer break provides a perfect opportunity to get outside. The problem with this argument is that most children aren't playing outside or even spending time with other kids. While some children visit summer camps, most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them.
The U.S. has changed from a farming economy to a knowledge- and innovation-based economy, so it makes sense for the school year to change as well.

关键。
【定位】But year-round schooling isn't just about academics. Teachers and students experience a
closer relationship in year-round schools than they do in traditional schools and, in the
absence of any long-term break, students do not feel detached from the school environment.
但全年制不仅仅关乎学业。在全年制学校里，师生关系比在传统学校里更亲近，而且由于没
有任何长期假期，学生不会感到与校园环境疏离。
【选项】A) 答非所问
get back to where their lessons started 套用第二段 get back to where they were，
那讲的是暑期遗忘后补回进度，属学业范畴，被题干限定排除，且原文是消除这一损耗
而非"帮学生回到起点"。
B) 答非所问
absorb what they have learned 仍是讲学习吸收，属 improving their learning 范
畴，被题干"除学业外"排除。
C) 偷换概念
原文说的是学生 do not feel detached from the school environment（不疏离），并
非 familiarize them with the school environment（使其熟悉环境），把"不疏远"偷
换成"变熟悉"。
D) ✓ 正确
Teachers and students experience a closer relationship ↔
strengthen their relationship with teachers
预判的"师生关系更近"正对应 strengthen their relationship with teachers，且它落
在"学业之外"的范围内，故选此项。

questions.stem: What do some childhood development experts believe about the long summer vacation?

options.label: A
options.text: It meets students' need to study on their own.

options.label: B
options.text: It enables students to learn about the outside world.

options.label: C
options.text: It satisfies students' desire to stay longer at home.

options.label: D
options.text: It contributes to students' healthy growth.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （细节题）
【判型】What do some childhood development experts believe about the long summer
vacation? 问的是专家在文中直接表述的观点，可逐字核对，不需要读者推断。
【拆句】Q53 主干 What do some childhood development experts believe，后接 about the
long summer vacation 点明评论对象；注意主语是 experts 而非作者，是"这话谁说的"的
关键。
【定位】Some childhood development experts believe that time off from school is vital to healthy
development as kids are not designed to spend so much of their time inside classrooms and
the summer break provides a perfect opportunity to get outside.
一些儿童发展专家认为，离开学校的休息时间对健康成长至关重要，因为孩子天生不适合把
这么多时间花在教室里，而暑假正好提供了走到户外的绝佳机会。
【选项】A) 无中生有

世界"。
C) 张冠李戴
专家观点里没有"满足学生 stay longer at home"的说法；待在家看电视是后文作者反驳
时提到的现实，并非专家所赞同的需求。
D) ✓ 正确
time off from school is vital to healthy development ↔
It contributes to students' healthy growth
预判的"放假利于健康成长"正对应 It contributes to students' healthy growth，故选
此项。

questions.explanation:
【答案】A （细节题）

在文中的具体反驳理由，可直接核对。
【拆句】Q54 主干 What is the argument against the experts' idea，介词 against 决定方向
是"反对专家"；读懂 against 才不会把专家自己的话误当反驳，是理解关键。
【定位】The problem with this argument is that most children aren't playing outside or even spending
time with other kids. While some children visit summer camps, most stay at home, watching
TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them.
这个论点的问题在于，大多数孩子并没有在户外玩耍，甚至没有和别的孩子相处。虽然有些
孩子去参加夏令营，但多数人待在家里看电视或玩电子设备上的游戏，这对他们几乎没有
好处。

most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits
them

playing outside 却把对象缩成"在外面玩的少数"，偷改了范围。
C) 无中生有

D) 以偏概全

I mean, how hard it could be to create fabric and  [26]  it into a shirt shape. Don't machines do all that? Well, creating fabric from cotton, which is the most  [27]  clothing material, is actually a process that involves a lot of water, 2,700 liters per shirt to be  [28]  . Take a look at the video below from National Geographic for some more mind-blowing  [29]  about cotton clothing production.

Clean water is  [30]  becoming one of the most sought-after resources in the world. Given how large the  [31]  and cotton industries are, they take up a lot of our fresh water demands across the world, according to The Huffington Post. The video from National Geographic was created to spread  [32]  of how environmentally harmful cotton is. But the situation can be made better. Through better water management and farming practices, water usage in cotton production can be cut down by  [33]  40 percent.

Called "Better Cotton", this environmentally conscious product will save millions of liters of water a year simply from  [34]  the demands of cotton production. questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】L) sew
动词
【词性槽】and 并列 + 不定式 to 后接动词原形
【依据】把布"缝"成衬衫形状，sew 最准
语境是 create fabric and __(26)__ it into a shirt shape——造出布料再把它"缝"成衬衫形
状，sew（缝制）正是做衣服的标准动作，与 into a shirt shape 搭配自然。
【竞争词】H) mend 义偏"修补"非"制作"
mend 是"修补"已破损的东西，这里是从布料"从无到有做成"衬衫，不是修补，方向不符。
M) shrink 义为"收缩"，逻辑反
shrink 是"使缩小"，"把布缩成衬衫形状"讲不通；而且 shrink 正是第 35 空"水供应减少"要用的
词，留给那里。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】B) abundant
形容词
【词性槽】the most + 空 + 名词，形容词最高级作定语
【依据】棉花是"最常见/产量最大"的衣料，abundant 最贴
句意是棉花作为 the most __(27)__ clothing material——最"丰富、大量"的衣料，与下文
one of the most useful cash crops across the globe 呼应，abundant（丰富的、大量
的）正合"用得最广"之意。
【竞争词】E) exact 搭配不成立
exact 意为"确切的"，"最确切的衣料"语义不通，exact 通常修饰数字、答案等，不能形容棉花作
为材料的普遍性。
G) intense 义不对
intense 是"强烈的、剧烈的"，形容情感、光线、竞争等，"最强烈的衣料"讲不通；它更可能去
配第 31 空那种"产业"语境，但此处不合。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】E) exact
形容词
【词性槽】to be + 空，系动词后作表语
【依据】"to be exact"=确切地说，是固定插入语
2,700 liters per shirt to be __(28)__ 在精确数字 2,700 liters 后用 "to be exact"（确切地
说）这一固定表达收尾，exact 修饰前面给出的精确数字，框架直接锁死。
【竞争词】G) intense 义不符且无此搭配
intense 是"强烈的"，"to be intense"在此说不通，也不是固定插入语；它形容情感/程度，
与"确切数字"语境无关。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】N) statistics
名词
【词性槽】some more + 空 + about，形容词后接名词
【依据】承接上句"2,700 升"的数字，statistics=统计数据最贴
前句刚给出 2,700 liters per shirt 这样的数字，叫人去看视频了解"更多令人震惊的数据"，
statistics（统计数据）与 mind-blowing、about cotton production 完全吻合。
【竞争词】C) awareness 义为"意识"，且被第 32 空占用
awareness 是"意识"，"更多令人震惊的意识"不通；它是第 32 空 spread ___ 的正解，留给
那里。
D) conscience 义为"良心"，与数据无关
conscience（良心、道德感）和"关于棉花生产的震撼信息"不搭，且不可用 some more 这样表
数量地修饰。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】F) increasingly
副词
【词性槽】is + 空 + becoming，插在系动词与现在分词之间
【依据】清洁水"日益"变得抢手，increasingly 表渐变正合
Clean water is __(30)__ becoming one of the most sought-after resources in the
world 描述一种正在加剧的趋势，increasingly（越来越、日益地）修饰 becoming 表渐
变，语义贴切。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】O) textile
名词
【词性槽】the + 空 + and cotton industries，定语名词
【依据】与 cotton 并列指"纺织业"，textile 正合
the __(31)__ and cotton industries——"纺织与棉花产业"，textile（纺织品/纺织的）和
cotton 同属衣料产业、并列自然，且 textile industry 是固定说法。
【竞争词】D) conscience 义为"良心"，不能与 cotton 并列指产业
conscience 是抽象"良心"，"良心和棉花产业"语义不搭，也不构成 ___ industry 这类产业名，
逻辑不成立。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】C) awareness
名词
【词性槽】spread + 空 + of，及物动词后作宾语
【依据】"spread awareness of"=传播……意识，固定搭配
spread __(32)__ of how environmentally harmful cotton is——视频是为了"传播对棉花
危害环境的认知"，spread awareness of 是高频固定搭配，awareness（意识、知晓）完
全契合。
【竞争词】D) conscience 形近义异，无此搭配
conscience（良心）与 awareness（意识）形近易混，但"spread conscience of"不成立，句意
是让人"知道"棉花的环境危害，是认知层面而非道德良心。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 D) —— conscience 与 awareness 形近、词性都对。spread
__(32)__ of how environmentally harmful cotton is：D\(conscience\) 和正解形近、同
为抽象名词，最易误选；防坑就背一句固定搭配"spread awareness of"。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】I) nearly
副词
【词性槽】空 + 40 percent，修饰数量的副词
【依据】修饰 40 percent 表"将近 40%"，nearly 最贴
cut down by __(33)__ 40 percent 说节水幅度"将近 40%"，nearly（将近、几乎）正是修
饰数字、表示接近某量的标准副词。
【竞争词】F) increasingly 义为"越来越"，不修饰固定数字
increasingly 表"日益、越来越"，描述渐变趋势，不能修饰 40 percent 这样的固定百分比；它
是第 30 空 ___ becoming 的正解。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】K) reducing
动词
【词性槽】介词 from 后接动名词
【依据】"减少需求"用 reducing，且现成-ing 形态
save millions of liters of water a year simply from __(34)__ the demands of cotton
production——靠"减少"棉花生产的需求来省水，reducing the demands 是地道及物搭
配，且词库直接给的就是-ing 形式，无需变形。
【竞争词】M) shrink 形态需变且与 demands 搭配弱
shrink 是原形，作动名词得改成 shrinking 才合 from 后位置，而词库取词须逐字、本无-ing
形；且 shrink 多指物体/数量自身收缩，"shrink the demands"不如"reduce the demands"地
道。shrink 正是第 35 空 as water supplies ___ 的答案，留给那里。
【易错】最具迷惑性的错误词是 M) —— shrink 也表"减少"、看着也通。第 34 空 from __(34)__
the demands：shrink 词义也是"减少"，易抢 reducing 的位置；防坑是"reduce the
demands"才是地道及物搭配，且 shrink 留给第 35 空。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.explanation:
【答案】M) shrink
动词
【词性槽】as 从句主语 supplies 后缺谓语
【依据】水供应"减少"，shrink 表自身缩减最贴
as water supplies __(35)__, farmers and consumers need to be more conscious 说"随
着水供应减少"，shrink（缩小、减少）正描述供应量自身收缩，与全文"清洁水日益稀
缺"呼应。

title: 2023年06月真题·第1套 · 长篇匹配（The spoken web）

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: We're growing more used to chatting to our computers, phones and smart speakers through voice assistants like Amazon's Alexa, Apple's Siri and Microsoft's Cortana. Blind and partially sighted people have been using text-to-speech converters for decades.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Out of these assistants, Siri is the most well-known. The assistant uses voice inquiries and a natural-language user interface(界面) to answer questions. The software adapts to users' individual language usages, searches, and preferences, with continuing use.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Some think voice could soon take over from typing and clicking as the main way to interact online. But what are the challenges of moving to "the spoken web"?

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: What use is written online content if you can't read? That is the situation facing illiterate(不识字的) African farmers. They are often denied crucial information the web offers many others. With a literacy rate in some parts of Africa at only 22.6%, farmers are often "underpaid for their produce because they might be unaware of the prevailing prices," says Francis Dittoh, a researcher behind Mr Meteo, a speech-based weather information service.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "The most frequently heard complaint is about rainfall predictions," says Mr Dittoh, who lives in Tamale, northern Ghana. "They tell us the methods their forefathers used to predict the weather don't seem to work as well these days." This is down to climate change, he believes. Yet knowing when it's going to rain is vital for farmers wanting to sow seeds, irrigate crops or take their animals out to the fields to feed on grass.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Mr Dittoh says the idea of converting online weather reports into speech came from the farmers themselves, after a workshop in the village of Guabuligah. "They came up with this," he says. Mr Meteo takes the online weather forecast, converts it to a short recording in the appropriate language and makes it available on a basic phone. Farmers ring up to receive the information. The local language Dagbani is spoken by 1.2 million people but is not served by any online translation applications. The service was designed to be cheap and easy to run, says Mr Dittoh. He plans to begin field tests this month, working with Tamale's Savanna Agricultural Research Institute.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The spoken web could also help the one-in-five adults in Europe and the U.S. with poor reading skills. But building the spoken web—web-to-voice and voice-to-web—isn't straightforward. For software to understand that pizza is served at Italian restaurants is easy. To cover multiple domains and to be able to have a conversation with users on every single topic is still a long way off.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: So although many computer assistants can answer simple questions about the weather and play music for us, anything resembling a wide-ranging human conversation is decades away. Artificial intelligence just isn't smart enough yet. Even turning your voice into text—automatic speech recognition—is one of the hardest problems to solve, as there are as many ways to pronounce things as there are people on the planet.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Siri has often been praised for its ability to interpret our casual language and deliver very specific and accurate results, sometimes even providing additional information. But it is still somewhat restricted, particularly when the language moves away from stiffer commands into more human interactions. In one example, the phrase "Send a text to Jason, Clint, Sam, and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant" was interpreted as sending a message to Jason only, containing the text "Clint Sam and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant". It has also been noted that Siri lacks a proper editing function, as saying "Edit message to say: we're at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us" generates "Clint Sam and Lee saying we're having dinner at Silver Cloud restaurant to say we're at Silver Cloud restaurant and you should come find us".

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Using voice interaction feels far more intimate than surfing the net the old-fashioned way. This is intentional as the informal tone of the assistant helps create an emotional attachment. But if something speaks, it must also listen. Our phones are always near us and they are collecting data about us all the time. This has already raised privacy concerns. The American Civil Liberties Union has stated that digital assistants create a threat to privacy from hackers. Some people have other concerns. They worry assistants will one day be used to deliver advertising directly to us.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: But digital voices need more personality to make them popular. Robots are not yet witty, Siri is boring. The benefits of using voice instead of tapping fingers obviously depend on the context. Doctors completing online forms about their patients by speech, for example, can dictate 150 words a minute, three times faster than typing on a keyboard. This enables them to spend less time on administration and more time with patients.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Last year, speech recognition company Nuance helped a doctors' surgery in Dukinfield, near Manchester, set up a speech system for the practice's six doctors. Now they can dictate notes on a patient's health condition and treatment and a smart assistant automatically enters the information into the right fields on a web form. Previously, the doctors made voice recordings that were then transcribed by secretaries—a process that was costly and likely to cause delays. The new system means letters to patients now have more detail.

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: Using voice also makes sense when you're doing other things with your hands. Think about when you're cooking, and you just want to know what the next step in the recipe is. Your hands are covered with oil; you're not going to get on the iPad, so it's a lot more natural to talk. And speech obviously makes sense when you're driving. In the U.S., 29% of drivers admit they surf behind the wheel, according to insurance firm State Farm. This is up from 13% in 2009. No wonder using mobile phones while driving causes more crashes a year than drink driving, says the U.S. National Safety Council.

questions.stem: According to Francis Dittoh, their speech-based weather information service was meant to be inexpensive and easy to use.
questions.explanation:
【答案】F 段（强锚点）
【锚点】便宜易用的天气服务
【定位】The service was designed to be cheap and easy to run, says Mr Dittoh.
这项服务被设计得便宜又易于运行，Dittoh 先生说。
【改写】inexpensive and easy to use ↔ cheap and easy to run
便宜易用同义替换
their speech-based weather information service ↔
Mr Meteo takes the online weather forecast, converts it to a short recording
服务名与其描述对应
【辨邻】 D D 段借 Dittoh 之口讲农民 underpaid for their produce 的困境，并未提服务"便宜易
用"，不是本句源头。
says Francis Dittoh, a researcher behind Mr Meteo, a speech-based weather information service
questions.locateHint: The service was designed to be cheap and easy to run, says Mr Dittoh.

questions.stem: Using voice instead of typing enables doctors to spend more time taking care of patients.
questions.explanation:
【答案】K 段（强锚点）

title: 2023年06月真题·第1套 · 仔细阅读 Passage 1

paragraphs.text: The United States is facing a housing crisis: Affordable housing is inadequate, while luxury homes abound(充裕), and homelessness remains a persistent problem. Despite this, popular culture and the housing industry market happiness as living with both more space and more amenities(便利设施). Big houses are advertised as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury.

This is reflected in our homes. The average single-family home built in the United States before 1970 was less than 1,500 square feet in size. By 2016, the average size of a new, single-family home was 2,422 square feet. What's more, homes built in the 2000s were more likely than earlier models to have more of all types of spaces: bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms, dining rooms, recreation rooms and garages.

There are consequences of living big. As middle-class houses have grown larger, two things have happened. First, large houses take time to maintain, so cleaners and other low-wage service workers are required to keep these houses in order. Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. Take swimming pools. While in 1950, only 2,500 U.S. families owned pools, by 1999 this number was 4 million. At the same time, public municipal pools were often closed, leaving low-income people nowhere to swim.

The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. Should Americans accept a system in which the middle and upper classes enjoy a luxurious lifestyle, using the low-wage labor of others? Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor?

I believe neither is acceptable. We must change the way we think: living well does not need to mean having more private spaces; instead, it could mean having more public spaces. A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all.

paragraphs.text: Most of us in the entrepreneurial community are blessed—or cursed—with higher-than-average ambition. Ambitious people strongly desire accomplishments and are willing to take more risks and spend more effort to get them.
Overall, this is a positive quality, especially for people trying to build their own businesses. Apparently, if you're more naturally driven to set goals, you are more likely to succeed.
Actually, this isn't always the case. In fact, in some cases, extreme ambition may end up doing more harm than good.

One major side effect of excessive ambition is the tendency to focus too determinedly on one particular vision or end goal. This is problematic because it hinders your ability to adapt to new circumstances, which is vital if you want to be a successful entrepreneur. If a new competitor emerges to threaten your business, you may need to change direction, even if that means straying from your original vision. If you have too much ambition, you'll find this hard, if not impossible.
Few people are successful when they try to build their first brand. Unfortunately, for the most ambitious entrepreneurs, a failure is seen as disastrous, and impossible to recover from.

It's a clear departure from the intended plan toward the intended goal. For people with limited ambition, however, failure is viewed as something closer to reality. Remember, failure is inevitable, and every failure you survive is a learning experience.

Ambitious people tend to be more materialistically successful than their non-ambitious counterparts. However, they're only slightly happier than their less-ambitious counterparts, and tend to live significantly shorter lives. This implies that even though ambitious people are more likely to achieve conventional "success," such success means nothing for their health and happiness—and if you don't have health and happiness, what else could possibly matter?

Clearly, some amount of ambition is good for your motivation. Without any ambition, you wouldn't start your own business, set or achieve goals and get far in life. But an excess of ambition can also be dangerous, putting you at risk of burnout, stubbornness and even a shorter life.

【答案】A （词义句意题）
【判型】题干 What does the author imply by saying "this isn't always the case" 用 imply by
saying 问一个具体句子的含义，要求理解 this 指代什么、否定的是什么，属词义句意题。
【拆句】题干主干 What does the author imply，by saying "..." 是方式状语；关键在引文里的
this 是指代词，须回原文找它替代的上文内容；isn't always 是部分否定，意为"并非总
是"，不是全盘否定。
【定位】Actually, this isn't always the case.
实际上，情况并非总是如此。
【选项】A) ✓ 正确
you are more likely to succeed ↔ may not have a greater chance of success
选项 Ambitious people may not have a greater chance of success 正是"this（野心
者更易成功）＋部分否定"的还原，与预判一致。
B) 偷换概念
this 指代的是"更易成功"，并非"积极特质"；选项 may not have more positive
qualities 把否定矛头指向上一段的 positive quality，找错了 this 的指代。
C) 与原文相反
原文只说极端野心 may end up doing more harm than good（弊"大于"利），选项
却说 does as much good as harm（利害"相当"），把"大于"篡改成"相等"。
D) 与原文相反
选项 more naturally driven to success 几乎照搬上文 more naturally driven to set
goals，可这恰是本句要否定的观点，方向正好相反。

questions.stem: What does the author say is of extreme importance for one to become a successful entrepreneur?

questions.explanation:
【答案】B （细节题）
【判型】题干 What does the author say is of extreme importance 用 say 直问作者明说的内容，
答案是原文一句强调重要性的话，属细节题。
【拆句】题干 What does the author say is of extreme importance for one to become a
successful entrepreneur?，主干是 What...is of extreme importance；of+抽象名词等于
形容词，of extreme importance＝extremely important；for one to become... 是不定
式目的状语，指明"为了成为成功创业者"。
【定位】This is problematic because it hinders your ability to adapt to new circumstances, which is
vital if you want to be a successful entrepreneur.
这是有问题的，因为它会损害你适应新环境的能力，而这种能力对于想成为成功创业者的人
至关重要。
【选项】A) 与原文相反
原文说过度野心导致 focus too determinedly on one particular vision 反而有害，需
straying from your original vision；选项 Holding on to one's original vision（死守
原愿景）正是文章要批评的做法。
B) ✓ 正确
adapt to new circumstances ↔ adapt to new situations
选项 Being able to adapt to new situations 与预判"适应新环境的能力"几乎逐词对
应，确为答案。
C) 与原文相反
选项 Focusing determinedly on one particular goal 直接抄自 focus too
determinedly on one particular vision，而原文说这是过度野心的"副作用"，绝非"极
其重要"之事。
D) 与原文相反
原文说有时须 change direction"改变方向"，选项却说 Avoiding radical change in
one's career direction"避免大改方向"，与文意相左。

questions.stem: How do the most ambitious entrepreneurs regard failure in their endeavor?

options.label: A
options.text: It will awaken them to reality.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a lesson they have to learn.

options.label: C
options.text: It means the end of their career.

options.label: D
options.text: It will result in a slow recovery.

questions.explanation:
【答案】C （细节题）
【判型】题干 How do the most ambitious entrepreneurs regard failure 问一个明确群体对失败
的态度，原文有明文表述，属细节题。
【拆句】题干 How do the most ambitious entrepreneurs regard failure in their endeavor?，
regard sth 意为"看待某事"，in their endeavor（在其奋斗中）是范围状语；结构清晰、无
陷阱。
【定位】Unfortunately, for the most ambitious entrepreneurs, a failure is seen as disastrous, and
impossible to recover from.
不幸的是，对那些野心最大的创业者来说，一次失败被视为灾难性的、且无法翻身的。
【选项】A) 张冠李戴
awaken them to reality 对应的是第六段 failure is viewed as something closer to
reality，那讲的是"野心有限者"，而非题干问的"野心最大者"。
B) 张冠李戴
a lesson they have to learn 对应第六段 every failure you survive is a learning
experience，同样是说"野心有限者"，张冠李戴。
C) ✓ 正确
disastrous, and impossible to recover from ↔ means the end of their career
选项 It means the end of their career 把"灾难、无法恢复"提炼成"事业到头"，与预判
一致，确为答案。
D) 与原文相反
原文说 impossible to recover from"无法恢复"，选项却说 result in a slow
recovery"导致缓慢恢复"，恢复从"不可能"被偷改成"慢"。

questions.stem: What does the author advise us to do concerning ambition?

options.label: A
options.text: Distinguish between conventional success and our life goal.

options.label: B
options.text: Follow the example of the most ambitious entrepreneurs.

options.label: C
options.text: Avoid taking unnecessary risks when starting a business.

options.label: D
options.text: Prioritize health and happiness over material success.

questions.explanation:
【答案】D （推断题）
【判型】题干 What does the author advise us to do concerning ambition? 问作者的建议，原文
未必有一句直说"我建议你……"，需综合全文对野心利弊的论述提炼，属推断题。
【拆句】题干 What does the author advise us to do concerning ambition?，advise sb to do
意为"建议某人做某事"，concerning ambition（关于野心）是话题状语；结构平铺直叙、
无陷阱。
【选项】A) 偷换概念
原文要区分的是 conventional "success" 与 health and happiness，选项 Distinguish
between conventional success and our life goal 把后一项换成了文中没有的"人生目
标"，区分对象被改错。
B) 与原文相反
全文都在指出 the most ambitious entrepreneurs 看待失败的方式有害，选项 Follow
the example of the most ambitious entrepreneurs 却劝人效仿他们，与作者立场正
相反。
C) 以偏概全
Avoid taking unnecessary risks 只关乎 take more risks 这一点，并非全文劝诫的落
脚；作者最终落点是健康幸福，而非"少冒险"，以偏概全且无中生有。
D) ✓ 正确
such success means nothing for their health and happiness—and if you don't have health and
happiness, what else could possibly matter?
↔ Prioritize health and happiness over material success
选项 Prioritize health and happiness over material success 与主线"健康幸福重于成
功"吻合，且统摄全文对过度野心的批评，是建议题应有的全局答案。
